```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# ---- where this script lives -------------------------------------------------
# Every path below is relative to the folder holding this file, so the package
# runs from anywhere. That folder is found automatically when the document is
# KNITTED. Running chunks one at a time in an IDE, it cannot be: knitr has no
# current input, and the working directory is wherever the session happens to be.
#
# For that case, set CODE_DIR to the folder holding this file. Leave it empty
# for a normal knit.
#
# ============================================================================
# LOCAL RUN SETTINGS -- clear both before packaging for release:
#   1. CODE_DIR below  -> ""
#   2. DRAW in chunk 0 -> paste0(DATA_DIR, "raw/")
# ============================================================================
CODE_DIR = ""

rmd_file = tryCatch(knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE), error = function(e) NULL)
code_dir = if (nzchar(CODE_DIR)) {
  normalizePath(CODE_DIR, winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)
} else if (!is.null(rmd_file)) {
  dirname(normalizePath(rmd_file, winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE))
} else if (file.exists("work_dataframe.Rmd")) {
  normalizePath(getwd(), winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)
} else {
  stop(
    "Cannot locate this script's folder.\n",
    "  working directory: ", getwd(), "\n\n",
    "Either knit the document, or -- if you are running chunks one at a time --\n",
    "do ONE of:\n",
    '  * set CODE_DIR above to the folder holding work_dataframe.Rmd, or\n',
    '  * setwd("<package>/code") before running this chunk'
  )
}
stopifnot(file.exists(file.path(code_dir, "work_dataframe.Rmd")))

setwd(code_dir)
```

## 0. INITIALIZATION
```{r 0, include=FALSE}

# Number of workers for parallelization
max_workers = 9

# Name of DETER shapefile (update with your version)
DETER_zip = "INPE/deter-amz-public-2026mar29.zip"

# PRODES product must match the administrative study region.
PRODES_LAYER = "yearly_deforestation_amazonia_legal"
PRODES_zip = paste0("INPE/", PRODES_LAYER, ".zip")


# ---- data locations ----------------------------------------------------------
# Every path in this file is relative to the folder holding the script (set
# above). DATA_DIR is where this pipeline WRITES: intermediates and the analysis
# panels. Raw inputs are read from DRAW, set separately below.
DATA_DIR = "../data/"

# DV      intermediates. Rebuilt by this script, not committed.
# DFINAL  the two analysis panels and the other committed analysis inputs: what
#         starlink_results.Rmd reads, so a fresh clone can reproduce every table
#         without first running this pipeline.
DV = paste0(DATA_DIR, "processed/")
DFINAL = DATA_DIR

# DRAW    raw provider downloads, one folder per provider (see README section 2).
#         Set separately from DATA_DIR so the raw collection can live outside the
#         package -- a shared folder, an external drive, an existing archive --
#         while everything this pipeline WRITES still lands under DATA_DIR.
#         Absolute paths are fine. Examples:
#           DRAW = "D:/data/starlink-raw/"
#           DRAW = paste0(DATA_DIR, "raw/")   <- the shipped default
#
# CURRENTLY pointed at the shared project collection, which already holds every
# provider folder. Set it back to paste0(DATA_DIR, "raw/") before packaging.
DRAW = paste0(DATA_DIR, "raw/")

# The tenure system is a build-once input. Its diagnostics, SICAR state pieces
# and masks live here; the objects consumed by the rest of the pipeline are
# still written to DV as zones.RDS, sicar_area.RDS and overlap_area.RDS.
DS = paste0(DV, "tenures/")

# Create the folders this pipeline WRITES to. Raw folders are deliberately not
# created: they are user-supplied, and creating an empty one would turn a missing
# download into a silent empty read further down.
for (folder in c(DV, DS, DFINAL)) {
  if (!dir.exists(folder)) {
    dir.create(folder, recursive = TRUE)
    message("Created folder: ", folder)
  }
}

# ---- raw-source presence check ----------------------------------------------
# Fail here, by name, rather than hours into a run on an obscure path error.
# Each entry is a provider folder under data/raw/; README.md lists what belongs
# in each and where to download it.
raw_providers = c(
  "ANA", "ANATEL", "CAMS-EAC4", "CHC", "CNFP", "DATASUS", "DNIT", "FAO-GAEZ",
  "Copernicus", "FBSP", "FUNAI", "IBAMA", "IBGE", "ICMBio", "INCRA", "INPE", "MapBiomas",
  "SEAB-PR", "SICAR"
)
missing_raw = raw_providers[
  !dir.exists(file.path(DRAW, raw_providers)) |
    lengths(lapply(file.path(DRAW, raw_providers), list.files)) == 0
]
if (length(missing_raw) > 0) {
  stop(
    "Raw sources missing or empty under\n  DRAW = ", DRAW,
    "\n  resolving to ",
    tryCatch(normalizePath(DRAW, winslash = "/", mustWork = FALSE),
             error = function(e) "an unresolvable path"),
    "\n  from working directory ", getwd(),
    "\n\nMissing: ", paste(missing_raw, collapse = ", "),
    "\n\nIf every provider IS present somewhere else, point DRAW at it rather",
    "\nthan copying. README section 2 lists what each folder should contain."
  )
}
rm(raw_providers, missing_raw)

# Absolute twins of the two paths the SICAR builder uses inside parallel workers.
# A worker is a fresh R session and does not necessarily inherit this session's
# working directory, so a relative path can resolve somewhere else entirely --
# and the failure would surface hours into a run, as a missing file.
DS_ABS = paste0(normalizePath(DS, winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE), "/")
SICAR_DIR_ABS = normalizePath(paste0(DRAW, "SICAR"), winslash = "/",
                              mustWork = TRUE)


# Loading required R packages
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(readxl)
library(tiff)
library(stringi)
library(exactextractr)
library(terra)
library(future.apply)

# Official CRS for computing areas (SIRGAS 2000 - conic Albers equiv, in meters)
# https://biblioteca.ibge.gov.br/visualizacao/livros/liv102169.pdf (page 21)
proj_wk = 'PROJCS["Conica_Equivalente_de_Albers_Brasil",  
    GEOGCS["GCS_SIRGAS2000",  
      DATUM["D_SIRGAS2000",  
        SPHEROID["Geodetic_Reference_System_of_1980",6378137,298.2572221009113]],  
      PRIMEM["Greenwich",0],  
      UNIT["Degree",0.017453292519943295]],  
    PROJECTION["Albers"],  
    PARAMETER["standard_parallel_1",-2],  
    PARAMETER["standard_parallel_2",-22],  
    PARAMETER["latitude_of_origin",-12],  
    PARAMETER["central_meridian",-54],  
    PARAMETER["false_easting",5000000],  
    PARAMETER["false_northing",10000000],  
    UNIT["Meter",1]]'

# Function to obtain info of shapefiles/rasters' CRS/EPSG
crs_info = function(x) {
  crs_obj = st_crs(x)
  sprintf(
    "CRS: %s | EPSG: %s | Unit: %s",
    sub('^[^"]*"([^"]+)".*$', '\\1', crs_obj$wkt),
    crs_obj$epsg,
    crs_obj$units_gdal
  )
}

# ---- Mojui dos Campos / Santarem merge: constants and helpers ----------------
# Used by the amz merge just below, the within-boundary population block beside the
# population read, the legacy-zones guard after readRDS, and the codmun-keyed
# sources in sections 5, 8, 11 and A2. Section 99 guards that no stale
# pre-merge intermediate is ever joined.
MOJUI_CODMUN = 1504752
SANTAREM_CODMUN = 1506807

merge_codmun = function(x) ifelse(x == MOJUI_CODMUN, SANTAREM_CODMUN, x)

# Collapse Mojui's rows into Santarem's in a codmun-keyed table: numeric
# columns summed within `by` groups (by = "year" for panels), everything else
# keeps the first value. Other municipalities untouched; an all-NA pair stays
# NA. Used by the legacy-zones guard, sicar/overlap areas, and A2.
collapse_mojui = function(df, by = character(0)) {
  if (!"codmun" %in% names(df) || !any(df$codmun == MOJUI_CODMUN, na.rm = TRUE))
    return(df)
  hit = df$codmun %in% c(MOJUI_CODMUN, SANTAREM_CODMUN)
  sum_keep_na = function(x) if (all(is.na(x))) x[1] else sum(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  merged = df[hit, ] %>%
    group_by(across(all_of(by))) %>%
    summarise(
      across(where(is.numeric) & !any_of(c("codmun", by)), sum_keep_na),
      across(where(~ !is.numeric(.x)) & !any_of(c("codmun", by)), ~ first(.x)),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(codmun = SANTAREM_CODMUN)
  bind_rows(df[!hit, ], merged) %>% arrange(codmun)
}

# Original CLIPPED areas of the pair (km2, pre-merge panel values), for
# AREA-WEIGHTED merging of cached municipal MEANS built before the merge (PM
# caches in 6c, shm_ shares and forest stock in 9): collapse_mojui SUMS, which
# is right for areas and counts and WRONG for means and shares.
MOJUI_PAIR_W = tibble(codmun = c(SANTAREM_CODMUN, MOJUI_CODMUN),
                      w_area = c(18013.977, 4982.597))


# ---- fixed SICAR-stock parameters -------------------------------------------
SICAR_IOU = 0.95        # >= this share of shared area = the same footprint
SICAR_AREA_RATIO = 0.9  # declared-size prefilter for candidate pairs
SICAR_BBOX_RATIO = 0.5  # bounding-box overlap prefilter for candidate pairs

# Structural exclusion applied before the tenure masks are built.
SICAR_MAX_HA = 1e5        # a registration larger than this is not a property

# Groups of records that describe the same parcel: the connected components of
# the "is a duplicate of" relation. Union-find rather than a graph package, so
# the pipeline gains no dependency for fifteen lines of work. Every vertex is
# passed in, not just the ones with an edge, which is what makes a claim with
# no duplicate come out as its own group and an edgeless state work at all.
components_of = function(n, from, to) {
  parent = seq_len(n)
  find = function(x) {
    root = x
    while (parent[root] != root) root = parent[root]
    while (parent[x] != root) {          # path compression
      nxt = parent[x]
      parent[x] <<- root
      x = nxt
    }
    root
  }
  for (k in seq_along(from)) {
    a = find(from[k])
    b = find(to[k])
    if (a != b) parent[a] = b
  }
  roots = vapply(seq_len(n), find, numeric(1))
  match(roots, unique(roots))
}

ufs_sicar = c("AC", "AM", "AP", "MA", "MT", "PA", "RO", "RR", "TO")

# ============================================================================
# SICAR GEOMETRY HELPERS (pure functions used by the build-once block below).
# ============================================================================


# ---- geometry helpers, written to survive the awkward cases -----------------
# The recurring hazard is that sf represents "nothing left" in three different
# ways: a zero-length sfc, a length-one empty geometry, or a dropped feature.
# st_difference in particular RETURNS NOTHING for a feature it erases entirely,
# so a class that lies completely inside a higher-priority class would vanish
# from the output rather than appear as zero. Every helper below normalizes the
# empty case to one empty MULTIPOLYGON, which is what makes a municipality with
# no claims of some class come out as an honest zero.
EMPTY_MP = st_sfc(st_multipolygon(), crs = proj_wk)

is_nothing = function(g) {
  length(g) == 0 || all(st_is_empty(g))
}

# Everything that comes out of an overlay goes through here first. Two reasons,
# both found by running the AP state through this code.
#
# Differencing or intersecting shapes that share a boundary leaves a polygon
# with a stray line or point attached, wrapped in a GEOMETRYCOLLECTION. Casting
# one of those straight to MULTIPOLYGON is an error, and -- worse -- casting a
# MIXED set of collections and plain polygons succeeds while silently keeping
# only the first part of each collection, so land would go missing without any
# warning. Extracting the polygonal part first avoids both.
#
# The empty case is normalized to one empty MULTIPOLYGON, because sf otherwise
# expresses "nothing left" three different ways and a municipality with no
# claims of some class has to come out as an honest zero, not a dropped row.
as_mp = function(g) {
  if (is.null(g) || is_nothing(g)) return(EMPTY_MP)
  if (any(st_geometry_type(g) == "GEOMETRYCOLLECTION")) {
    g = st_collection_extract(g, "POLYGON")
  }
  g = g[st_geometry_type(g) %in% c("POLYGON", "MULTIPOLYGON")]
  if (is_nothing(g)) return(EMPTY_MP)
  out = tryCatch(st_make_valid(st_union(g)), error = function(e) {
    st_make_valid(st_union(st_make_valid(lwgeom::st_snap_to_grid(g, 0.01))))
  })
  if (is_nothing(out)) EMPTY_MP else st_cast(out, "MULTIPOLYGON", warn = FALSE)
}

u_or_empty = function(...) {
  as_mp(do.call(c, Filter(Negate(is.null), list(...))))
}

# Returns the difference, and a flag saying whether it actually happened. When
# both attempts fail the gross shape is kept rather than losing the
# municipality, but that means a "net" mask that still contains public land, so
# the caller records it and the builder reports every municipality where it
# occurred. A silent fallback here would be indistinguishable from a
# municipality that genuinely has no public land to net out.
safe_diff = function(x, y) {
  if (is_nothing(x) || is_nothing(y)) {
    return(list(g = if (is_nothing(x)) EMPTY_MP else x, failed = FALSE))
  }
  failed = FALSE
  out = tryCatch(
    st_make_valid(st_difference(x, y)),
    error = function(e) tryCatch(
      st_make_valid(st_difference(
        st_make_valid(lwgeom::st_snap_to_grid(x, 0.01)),
        st_make_valid(lwgeom::st_snap_to_grid(y, 0.01))
      )),
      error = function(e2) {
        failed <<- TRUE
        x
      }
    )
  )
  list(g = as_mp(out), failed = failed)
}

# Intersection kept only where it is a real piece of land: everything under
# 1 ha is dropped as boundary noise between two independently digitized layers.
safe_over = function(x, y, sliver_m2 = 1e4) {
  none = list(g = EMPTY_MP, n_drop = 0, a_drop = 0)
  if (is_nothing(x) || is_nothing(y)) return(none)
  o = tryCatch(st_make_valid(st_intersection(x, y)), error = function(e) {
    tryCatch(st_make_valid(st_intersection(
      st_make_valid(lwgeom::st_snap_to_grid(x, 0.01)),
      st_make_valid(lwgeom::st_snap_to_grid(y, 0.01))
    )), error = function(e2) EMPTY_MP)
  })
  o = as_mp(o)                     # one clean MULTIPOLYGON, or nothing
  if (is_nothing(o)) return(none)
  parts = tryCatch(st_cast(o, "POLYGON", warn = FALSE),
                   error = function(e) EMPTY_MP)
  if (is_nothing(parts)) return(none)
  a = as.numeric(st_area(parts))
  keep = a >= sliver_m2
  list(
    g = if (any(keep)) as_mp(parts[keep]) else EMPTY_MP,
    n_drop = sum(!keep),
    a_drop = sum(a[!keep])
  )
}

km2 = function(g) if (is_nothing(g)) 0 else sum(as.numeric(st_area(g))) / 1e6

# Clipping two polygon layers against each other can leave lines and points
# where boundaries merely touch, sometimes wrapped in a GEOMETRYCOLLECTION.
# They carry no area but do break a later union, so features are reduced to
# their polygonal part and the arealess ones are dropped.
# One row in, one row out, which is the whole point. st_collection_extract on a
# set of geometries SPLITS each collection into separate features -- feed it two
# collections holding three polygons between them and three geometries come
# back. Assigning that result into the rows it came from therefore recycles and
# silently puts one record's land on another record. So each collection is
# reduced on its own and its polygons combined into a single MULTIPOLYGON, and
# the geometry column is rebuilt rather than assigned into.
keep_polygons = function(x) {
  if (nrow(x) == 0) return(x)
  g = st_geometry(x)
  is_gc = st_geometry_type(g) == "GEOMETRYCOLLECTION"
  if (any(is_gc)) {
    crs_x = st_crs(g)
    g = st_sfc(lapply(seq_along(g), function(k) {
      if (!is_gc[k]) return(g[[k]])
      # warns when a collection holds no polygon at all, which is a normal
      # outcome here and handled by the branch below
      part = suppressWarnings(
        st_collection_extract(st_sfc(g[[k]], crs = crs_x), "POLYGON")
      )
      if (length(part) == 0 || all(st_is_empty(part))) {
        st_multipolygon()
      } else {
        st_combine(part)[[1]]
      }
    }), crs = crs_x)
    st_geometry(x) = g
  }
  x = x[st_geometry_type(st_geometry(x)) %in% c("POLYGON", "MULTIPOLYGON"), ]
  if (nrow(x) == 0) return(x)
  x[!st_is_empty(st_geometry(x)) &
      as.numeric(st_area(st_geometry(x))) > 0, ]
}


# ---- the tenure system ------------------------------------------------------
# Built from the raw SICAR registries and the public layers, every run. The
# products the rest of the pipeline consumes are zones.RDS, sicar_area.RDS and
# overlap_area.RDS; the per-state pieces and diagnostics stay under DS.

classify_sicar_stock = function(x) {
  module_ref = x %>%
    st_drop_geometry() %>%
    filter(!is.na(mod_fiscal), mod_fiscal > 0,
           !is.na(num_area), num_area > 0) %>%
    mutate(module_ha = num_area / mod_fiscal)

  module_by_mun = module_ref %>%
    group_by(uf, municipio) %>%
    summarise(module_ha = median(module_ha), .groups = "drop")

  module_by_uf = module_ref %>%
    group_by(uf) %>%
    summarise(module_uf = median(module_ha), .groups = "drop")

  x %>%
    left_join(module_by_mun, by = c("uf", "municipio")) %>%
    left_join(module_by_uf, by = "uf") %>%
    mutate(
      mf_used = ifelse(
        !is.na(mod_fiscal) & mod_fiscal > 0,
        mod_fiscal,
        num_area / coalesce(module_ha, module_uf)
      ),
      size_class = case_when(
        is.na(mf_used) | !is.finite(mf_used) | mf_used <= 0 ~ "unclassified",
        mf_used > 4 ~ "large",
        TRUE ~ "small"
      )
    ) %>%
    select(-module_ha, -module_uf)
}

build_sicar_stock_uf = function(uf, mun_zone) {
  zip = sprintf("%s/AREA_IMOVEL_%s.zip", SICAR_DIR_ABS, uf)
  d = st_read(paste0("/vsizip/", zip, "/AREA_IMOVEL_1.shp"), quiet = TRUE)
  n_read = nrow(d)

  # Restrict before the expensive geometry work. These are stock definitions,
  # not robustness filters: private rural registrations (IRU) present by 2021.
  d = d %>%
    mutate(
      uf = uf,
      cria = lubridate::dmy(dat_criaca, quiet = TRUE),
      mod_fiscal = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(mod_fiscal)),
      num_area = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(num_area))
    ) %>%
    filter(ind_tipo == "IRU", !is.na(cria), lubridate::year(cria) <= 2021)
  n_eligible = nrow(d)

  d = d %>%
    st_make_valid() %>%
    st_transform(crs = proj_wk) %>%
    lwgeom::st_snap_to_grid(0.01) %>%
    st_make_valid() %>%
    keep_polygons() %>%
    st_cast("MULTIPOLYGON", warn = FALSE) %>%
    mutate(
      area_m2 = as.numeric(st_area(st_geometry(.))),
      geom_ha = area_m2 / 1e4
    )
  n_polygonal = nrow(d)

  # Filter implausibly large geometries without retaining excluded records in
  # the submission package. The count remains in `stock_summary.RDS`.
  excluded = d %>% filter(geom_ha > SICAR_MAX_HA)
  d = d %>% filter(geom_ha <= SICAR_MAX_HA)
  n_excluded_large = nrow(excluded)
  n_after_size = nrow(d)

  # Exact duplicates share a geometry hash. Near duplicates are distinct
  # outlines whose intersection-over-union is at least SICAR_IOU.
  d$geom_hash = vapply(
    st_as_binary(st_geometry(d)), rlang::hash, character(1)
  )
  unique_shapes = d[!duplicated(d$geom_hash), ]
  shape_geom = st_geometry(unique_shapes)
  shape_area = unique_shapes$area_m2

  neighbours = st_intersects(unique_shapes)
  pairs = tibble::tibble(
    i = rep(seq_along(neighbours), lengths(neighbours)),
    j = unlist(neighbours)
  ) %>%
    filter(i < j)

  if (nrow(pairs) > 0) {
    pairs = pairs[
      pmin(shape_area[pairs$i], shape_area[pairs$j]) /
        pmax(shape_area[pairs$i], shape_area[pairs$j]) >= SICAR_AREA_RATIO,
      , drop = FALSE
    ]
  }

  if (nrow(pairs) > 0) {
    boxes = matrix(unlist(lapply(shape_geom, st_bbox)), ncol = 4, byrow = TRUE)
    box_width = pmax(
      0,
      pmin(boxes[pairs$i, 3], boxes[pairs$j, 3]) -
        pmax(boxes[pairs$i, 1], boxes[pairs$j, 1])
    )
    box_height = pmax(
      0,
      pmin(boxes[pairs$i, 4], boxes[pairs$j, 4]) -
        pmax(boxes[pairs$i, 2], boxes[pairs$j, 2])
    )
    box_area = (boxes[, 3] - boxes[, 1]) * (boxes[, 4] - boxes[, 2])
    pairs = pairs[
      box_width * box_height /
        pmax(box_area[pairs$i], box_area[pairs$j]) >= SICAR_BBOX_RATIO,
      , drop = FALSE
    ]
  }

  if (nrow(pairs) > 0) {
    pairs$iou = mapply(function(i, j) {
      intersection_area = tryCatch(
        sum(as.numeric(st_area(st_sfc(
          st_intersection(shape_geom[[i]], shape_geom[[j]]), crs = proj_wk
        )))),
        error = function(e) NA_real_
      )
      intersection_area /
        (shape_area[i] + shape_area[j] - intersection_area)
    }, pairs$i, pairs$j)
  } else {
    pairs$iou = numeric(0)
  }

  duplicate_edges = pairs %>%
    filter(!is.na(iou), iou >= SICAR_IOU)
  unique_shapes$footprint_id = paste0(
    uf, "_",
    components_of(nrow(unique_shapes), duplicate_edges$i, duplicate_edges$j)
  )

  d = d %>%
    left_join(
      unique_shapes %>%
        st_drop_geometry() %>%
        select(geom_hash, footprint_id),
      by = "geom_hash"
    )

  # Status is decided at the footprint level. A footprint is canceled only when
  # every registration on it is canceled. Canceled claims stay in their own
  # diagnostic mask but do not enter the live small- or large-property masks.
  footprint_status = d %>%
    st_drop_geometry() %>%
    group_by(footprint_id) %>%
    summarise(
      cancelled = all(!is.na(ind_status) & ind_status == "CA"),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  d = d %>%
    group_by(footprint_id) %>%
    arrange(cria, cod_imovel, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
    slice(1) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    left_join(footprint_status, by = "footprint_id") %>%
    classify_sicar_stock()

  # A current TO registry file contains one retained polygon with both declared
  # area and fiscal modules recorded as zero. Its geometry is only 0.052 m2, so
  # it is boundary noise rather than a classifiable rural property. Drop only
  # sub-square-meter unclassified artifacts; any material footprint with missing
  # size information must still stop the run.
  d = d %>%
    filter(!(size_class == "unclassified" & area_m2 < 1))
  if (any(d$size_class == "unclassified")) {
    stop(uf, ": fiscal-module size is missing for ",
         sum(d$size_class == "unclassified"), " retained footprints")
  }

  # Match the accepted mask build: a fully canceled footprint is evidence of an
  # attempted claim, but it is not a live small or large property in the study
  # window. Keeping it as class `ca` preserves the canceled-claim mask without
  # inflating the two property masks.
  d = d %>%
    mutate(size_class = ifelse(cancelled, "ca", size_class))

  pieces = d %>%
    select(footprint_id, cod_imovel, size_class, cancelled, mf_used, area_m2) %>%
    st_intersection(mun_zone) %>%
    st_make_valid() %>%
    keep_polygons()
  saveRDS(pieces, paste0(DS_ABS, "stock_pieces_", uf, ".RDS"))

  tibble::tibble(
    uf = uf,
    n_read = n_read,
    n_iru_through_2021 = n_eligible,
    n_polygonal = n_polygonal,
    n_excluded_large = n_excluded_large,
    n_exact_duplicates = n_after_size - nrow(unique_shapes),
    n_near_duplicate_edges = nrow(duplicate_edges),
    n_footprints = nrow(d),
    n_small = sum(d$size_class == "small"),
    n_large = sum(d$size_class == "large"),
    n_cancelled_flag = sum(d$cancelled)
  )
}

build_sicar_masks_shard = function(shard) {
  pieces = readRDS(paste0(DS_ABS, "stock_shard_", shard, ".RDS"))
  public = readRDS(paste0(DS_ABS, "public_layers.RDS"))

  lapply(sort(unique(pieces$codmun)), function(codmun_i) {
    p = pieces[pieces$codmun == codmun_i, ]
    gross_small = u_or_empty(st_geometry(p)[p$size_class == "small"])
    gross_large = u_or_empty(st_geometry(p)[p$size_class == "large"])
    cancelled = u_or_empty(st_geometry(p)[p$cancelled])

    public_mun = lapply(public, function(layer) {
      u_or_empty(st_geometry(layer)[layer$codmun == codmun_i])
    })
    any_public = u_or_empty(
      public_mun$ndpf, public_mun$ti, public_mun$uc, public_mun$sett
    )

    net_small = safe_diff(gross_small, any_public)
    net_large = safe_diff(gross_large, any_public)
    all_private = u_or_empty(gross_small, gross_large)

    overlap = lapply(
      public_mun,
      function(layer) safe_over(all_private, layer)
    )
    # The paper uses claim-size splits only inside undesignated public forests.
    # `safe_over()` dissolves each intersection to one MULTIPOLYGON, so a DETER
    # feature can be counted at most once within each reported size category.
    overlap_ndpf_large = safe_over(gross_large, public_mun$ndpf)
    overlap_ndpf_small = safe_over(gross_small, public_mun$ndpf)

    list(
      codmun = codmun_i,
      geoms = list(
        sicar21_small = net_small$g,
        sicar21_large = net_large$g,
        sicar21_ca = cancelled,
        sicarS21 = gross_small,
        sicarL21 = gross_large,
        over_ndpf = overlap$ndpf$g,
        over_ti = overlap$ti$g,
        over_uc = overlap$uc$g,
        over_sett = overlap$sett$g,
        over_ndpf_large = overlap_ndpf_large$g,
        over_ndpf_small = overlap_ndpf_small$g
      ),
      area = tibble::tibble(
        codmun = codmun_i,
        areasicar21_small = km2(net_small$g),
        areasicar21_large = km2(net_large$g),
        areasicar21_small_g = km2(gross_small),
        areasicar21_large_g = km2(gross_large),
        areasicar21_ca = km2(cancelled),
        areaover_ndpf = km2(overlap$ndpf$g),
        areaover_ti = km2(overlap$ti$g),
        areaover_uc = km2(overlap$uc$g),
        areaover_sett = km2(overlap$sett$g),
        areaover_ndpf_large = km2(overlap_ndpf_large$g),
        areaover_ndpf_small = km2(overlap_ndpf_small$g)
      ),
      net_failed = net_small$failed || net_large$failed
    )
  })
}

future::plan(
  future::multisession,
  workers = min(max_workers, N_SICAR_SHARDS)
)
tictoc::tic("fixed 2021 SICAR masks")
masks = future.apply::future_lapply(
  seq_len(N_SICAR_SHARDS),
  build_sicar_masks_shard,
  future.seed = TRUE,
  future.packages = c("sf", "dplyr", "lwgeom")
) %>%
  unlist(recursive = FALSE)
tictoc::toc()
future::plan(future::sequential)

codmuns_built = vapply(masks, `[[`, numeric(1), "codmun")
stopifnot(!any(duplicated(codmuns_built)))
if (any(vapply(masks, `[[`, logical(1), "net_failed"))) {
  warning("SICAR netting failed in at least one municipality; inspect masks")
}

mask_names = c(
  "sicar21_small", "sicar21_large", "sicar21_ca", "sicarS21", "sicarL21",
  "over_ndpf", "over_ti", "over_uc", "over_sett",
  "over_ndpf_large", "over_ndpf_small"
)
mask_sf = lapply(setNames(mask_names, mask_names), function(mask_name) {
  keep = Filter(function(x) !is_nothing(x$geoms[[mask_name]]), masks)
  if (length(keep) == 0) return(NULL)
  out = st_sf(
    codmun = vapply(keep, `[[`, numeric(1), "codmun"),
    geometry = do.call(c, lapply(keep, function(x) x$geoms[[mask_name]])),
    crs = proj_wk
  )
  stopifnot(nrow(out) == n_distinct(out$codmun), !any(st_is_empty(out)))
  out
})

for (mask_name in mask_names) {
  if (!is.null(mask_sf[[mask_name]])) {
    saveRDS(mask_sf[[mask_name]], paste0(DS_ABS, "mask_", mask_name, ".RDS"))
  }
}

sicar_area_new = mun_zone %>%

stopifnot(
  nrow(sicar_area_new) == 772,

        sicar_area_new$areasicar21_small_g + 1e-6),

        sicar_area_new$areasicar21_large_g + 1e-6)
)
overlap_area_new = sicar_area_new %>%

zones_new = c(
  unname(base_zones),
  lapply(mask_names, function(mask_name) {

) %>%

saveRDS(sicar_area_new, paste0(DS_ABS, "sicar_area.RDS"))
saveRDS(overlap_area_new, paste0(DS_ABS, "overlap_area.RDS"))

# ---- population within the Legal Amazon portion of each municipality ---------
# The Legal Amazon boundary cuts 21 Maranhao municipalities: for those the
# municipal polygon carries only part of the territory the 2022 census counted,
# so the full census population would overstate density. Their population inside
# the panel boundary is estimated by areal interpolation -- overlay the clipped
# polygon with the 2022 census tracts and give it each tract's population in
# proportion to the tract area it covers, summed over every overlapping tract,
# whatever municipality the tract is labelled with. Every other municipality
# keeps its census population unchanged: there the census value is the truth and
# an overlay could only add mesh noise. Assumes uniform population density
# within a tract, as any areal interpolation does.
#
# Maranhao is the only state that can be cut -- the Legal Amazon takes the other
# eight whole. The two raw census products are fetched once if absent and kept
# under their original IBGE names.
#
# Build-once: the 21-row result is cached because the overlay is slow and its
# inputs never change. Delete the cache to rebuild.
mun_pos = which(zones_prefixes == "mun")
stopifnot(length(mun_pos) == 1)
mun_poly = zones[[mun_pos]]$zone
municipal_population = mun_poly %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  select(codmun, pop)

partial_population_path = paste0(DV, "pop_clipped_21.RDS")
population_cache_path = paste0(DV, "pop_clipped.RDS")

if (!file.exists(partial_population_path)) {
  CENSUS_DIR = paste0(DRAW, "IBGE/")
  MA_MESH = paste0(CENSUS_DIR, "MA_setores_CD2022.gpkg")
  AGG_ZIP = paste0(CENSUS_DIR, "Agregados_por_setores_basico_BR_20260520.zip")

  fetch_once = function(url, dest, min_bytes = 1e5) {
    if (file.exists(dest) && file.size(dest) > min_bytes) return(invisible(TRUE))
    cat("fetching", basename(dest), "...\n")
    download.file(url, dest, mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE, method = "libcurl")
  }
  fetch_once(
    paste0("https://geoftp.ibge.gov.br/organizacao_do_territorio/",
           "malhas_territoriais/malhas_de_setores_censitarios__divisoes_",
           "intramunicipais/censo_2022/setores/gpkg/UF/MA/MA_setores_CD2022.gpkg"),
    MA_MESH)
  # Definitive aggregates (2026-05-20), NOT the 2024-03 preliminaries.
  fetch_once(
    paste0("https://ftp.ibge.gov.br/Censos/Censo_Demografico_2022/",
           "Agregados_por_Setores_Censitarios/Agregados_por_Setor_csv/",
           "Agregados_por_setores_basico_BR_20260520.zip"),
    AGG_ZIP)

  # Tract population (v0001), read straight from the zip -- nothing extracted.
  # Maranhao only; a tract's first two digits are its UF.
  csv_in_zip = utils::unzip(AGG_ZIP, list = TRUE)$Name
  csv_in_zip = csv_in_zip[grepl("[.]csv$", csv_in_zip, ignore.case = TRUE)][1]
  setor_pop = readr::read_delim(
    unz(AGG_ZIP, csv_in_zip), delim = ";", quote = "\"",
    locale = readr::locale(encoding = "latin1", decimal_mark = ","),
    col_types = readr::cols(.default = readr::col_character()),
    progress = FALSE) %>%
    transmute(CD_SETOR = as.character(CD_SETOR),
              pop_setor = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(v0001))) %>%
    filter(substr(CD_SETOR, 1, 2) == "21") %>%
    mutate(pop_setor = coalesce(pop_setor, 0))

  ma_tracts = st_read(MA_MESH, quiet = TRUE) %>%
    select(CD_SETOR, CD_MUN) %>%
    st_make_valid() %>%
    st_transform(proj_wk)
  # st_area on the sf OBJECT, not a named column: the gpkg's geometry column is
  # `geom`, not `geometry`, so referencing it by name errors.
  ma_tracts$tract_area = as.numeric(st_area(ma_tracts))

  # Which municipalities are cut? The tract mesh tiles whole municipalities, so
  # it supplies the full territory and no external area reference is needed:
  # clipped_share = clipped polygon area / summed tract area. Mesh disagreement
  # between the two products puts noise on both sides of 1, and shares ABOVE 1
  # are impossible (no clipping enlarges a polygon), so the noise floor is read
  # off the upper tail and the cut-off sits symmetrically below 1, doubled for
  # safety.
  ma_share = mun_poly %>%
    filter(codmun %/% 100000 == 21) %>%
    mutate(area_clipped_km2 = as.numeric(st_area(.)) / 1e6) %>%
    st_drop_geometry() %>%
    select(codmun, area_clipped_km2) %>%
    left_join(
      ma_tracts %>%
        st_drop_geometry() %>%
        group_by(codmun = as.numeric(CD_MUN)) %>%
        summarise(area_full_km2 = sum(tract_area) / 1e6, .groups = "drop"),
      by = "codmun"
    ) %>%
    mutate(clipped_share = area_clipped_km2 / area_full_km2)
  excess = ma_share$clipped_share[ma_share$clipped_share > 1]
  cut_threshold = 1 - max(quantile(excess, .99, na.rm = TRUE) - 1, 0.02) * 2
  cut_ids = ma_share$codmun[!is.na(ma_share$clipped_share) &
                              ma_share$clipped_share < cut_threshold]
  cat(sprintf("cut-off %.3f -> %d MA municipalities treated as cut\n",
              cut_threshold, length(cut_ids)))
  stopifnot(length(cut_ids) == 21)

  cut_polys = mun_poly %>%
    filter(codmun %in% cut_ids) %>%
    select(codmun)
  pop_ma = st_intersection(
    ma_tracts[lengths(st_intersects(ma_tracts, cut_polys)) > 0,
              c("CD_SETOR", "tract_area")],
    cut_polys)
  # same gpkg column-name issue as above: area from the object itself
  pop_ma$a_in = as.numeric(st_area(pop_ma))
  pop_ma = pop_ma %>%
    st_drop_geometry() %>%
    group_by(codmun, CD_SETOR, tract_area) %>%
    summarise(a_in = sum(a_in), .groups = "drop") %>% # multipart pieces
    mutate(ashare = pmin(1, a_in / tract_area)) %>%
    left_join(setor_pop, by = "CD_SETOR") %>%
    mutate(pop_setor = coalesce(pop_setor, 0)) %>%
    group_by(codmun) %>%
    summarise(pop_areawt = sum(pop_setor * ashare), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(pop_areawt = ceiling(pop_areawt))

  stopifnot(nrow(pop_ma) == 21, !anyNA(pop_ma$pop_areawt))
  saveRDS(pop_ma, partial_population_path)

  rm(setor_pop, ma_tracts, ma_share, excess, cut_threshold, cut_ids, cut_polys,
     pop_ma, csv_in_zip, CENSUS_DIR, MA_MESH, AGG_ZIP, fetch_once)
}

partial_population = readRDS(partial_population_path) %>%
  select(codmun, pop_areawt)

stopifnot(
  nrow(partial_population) == 21,
  !anyDuplicated(partial_population$codmun),
  all(partial_population$codmun %in% municipal_population$codmun)
)

population_legal_amazon = municipal_population %>%
  left_join(partial_population, by = "codmun") %>%
  mutate(
    is_cut = !is.na(pop_areawt),
    pop_areawt = ifelse(is.na(pop_areawt), pop, pop_areawt),
    clipped_pop_share = pop_areawt / pop
  ) %>%
  select(codmun, pop_areawt, clipped_pop_share, is_cut)

stopifnot(
  nrow(population_legal_amazon) == 772,
  sum(population_legal_amazon$is_cut) == 21,
  !anyNA(population_legal_amazon$pop_areawt)
)
saveRDS(population_legal_amazon, population_cache_path)

rm(
  partial_population_path,
  population_cache_path,
  mun_pos,
  mun_poly,
  municipal_population,
  partial_population,
  population_legal_amazon
)


# ============================================================================
# CONCENTRATION & DISPERSION HELPERS (pure functions; defined in INITIALIZATION
# so they are available to every downstream chunk -- DETER concentration in
# section 2 and fire-ignition concentration/dispersion in section 10).
# ============================================================================
# ============================================================================
# Within-year TEMPORAL concentration and SPATIAL dispersion of fire activity.
# Spec-of-record: notes/concentration_measures_reference.md (formulas, ranges,
# citations, design decisions).
# These are pure helpers (defined once, before the data chunks that call them).
# ============================================================================

# Low-count handling: a concentration index from very few events is sampling
# noise (e.g. 3 fires on 3 days -> max1 = HHI = 1/3 purely from small n). Rather
# than blank those rows here, the panels KEEP every municipality-year that has at
# least one event, carrying the raw indices plus the event count (conc_*_n /
# disp_n). The low-count threshold is then applied at ANALYSIS time as a sample
# filter on that count (see the ConcentrationDispersion chunk in
# starlink_results_v2.Rmd), so it can be swept (20/25/30, or 0 = none) without
# rebuilding the panel, and the full distribution stays inspectable.

# Sum weights `w` into `nbins` integer bins indexed by `id` (1..nbins); zeros kept.
tabulate_w = function(id, w, nbins) {
  out = numeric(nbins)
  agg = tapply(w, id, sum)
  out[as.integer(names(agg))] = as.numeric(agg)
  out
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# concentration_year(): all temporal-concentration indices for ONE
# municipality-year, at a fixed temporal bin width.
#   doy      integer day-of-(fire)year, 1..n_days (one value per EVENT row)
#   fmonth   calendar month 1..12 (used only for the "month" bin variant)
#   w        weight per event: 1 for counts; per-event area (km^2) for the area series
#   n_days   length of this fire-year (365 or 366), constant within the group
#   bin      bin width in days (1/7/15) OR the string "month" (12 calendar months)
#   is_count TRUE -> emit bias-corrected HHI_unb; FALSE (continuous area) -> NA
# Top-k shares are always DAY-based; HHI/Gini use the chosen bin; R-bar is bin-free.
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
concentration_year = function(doy, fmonth, w, n_days, bin = 1L, is_count = TRUE) {
  M    = sum(w)
  ntot = length(doy)                       # number of events in this munic-year

  # ---- top-k busiest DAYS (daily resolution, mass-weighted) ------------------
  day_mass = tabulate_w(doy, w, n_days)
  top  = sort(day_mass, decreasing = TRUE)
  max1 = top[1] / M
  max3 = sum(top[seq_len(min(3L, length(top)))]) / M
  max7 = sum(top[seq_len(min(7L, length(top)))]) / M

  # ---- peak CONSECUTIVE k-day window shares (mass in the busiest k-day run) ---
  # Windowed analog of max3/max7: a multi-day fire deposits mass on consecutive
  # days (fire spreads over days), which the order-blind top-k can split across
  # the calendar. max{3,7}w sum the heaviest CONSECUTIVE k-day run instead, so
  # one physical burst is read as one episode. Linear (non-wrapping) window --
  # Amazon fire season is mid-year, so the Dec->Jan boundary carries ~no mass.
  roll_peak = function(x, k) {               # max sum over any consecutive-k window
    if (length(x) <= k) return(sum(x))       # series shorter than window: whole-year sum
    cs = cumsum(c(0, x))
    max(cs[(k + 1L):length(cs)] - cs[seq_len(length(cs) - k)])
  }
  max3w = roll_peak(day_mass, 3L) / M
  max7w = roll_peak(day_mass, 7L) / M

  # ---- bins for HHI / Gini ---------------------------------------------------
  if (is.character(bin)) {                 # "month" -> 12 calendar-month bins
    bin_id = fmonth
    n_bins = 12L
  } else {
    n_bins = as.integer(ceiling(n_days / bin))
    bin_id = ((doy - 1L) %/% as.integer(bin)) + 1L
  }
  bin_mass = tabulate_w(bin_id, w, n_bins)

  s   = bin_mass / M
  hhi = sum(s^2)
  if (is_count) {
    # Unbiased Simpson: bin_mass are integer counts (w == 1). See ref-note sec.3.
    hhi_unb = if (M > 1) sum(bin_mass * (bin_mass - 1)) / (M * (M - 1)) else NA_real_
  } else {
    hhi_unb = NA_real_                     # undefined for continuous area mass
  }

  # ---- Gini over the full zero-filled set of bins ----------------------------
  xs   = sort(bin_mass)
  idx  = seq_along(xs)
  gini = (2 * sum(idx * xs)) / (n_bins * sum(xs)) - (n_bins + 1) / n_bins

  # ---- bin-free circular resultant length (rotation-invariant) ---------------
  th   = 2 * pi * doy / n_days
  rbar = sqrt(sum(w * cos(th))^2 + sum(w * sin(th))^2) / M

  data.frame(
    n_events = ntot, mass = M,
    max1 = max1, max3 = max3, max7 = max7,
    max3w = max3w, max7w = max7w,
    hhi = hhi, hhi_unb = hhi_unb, gini = gini, rbar = rbar
  )
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# rarefy_year(): Hurlbert-style rarefied (count-robust) indices for ONE
# municipality-year. Averages max1/max3/max7/gini over B subsamples of m events
# drawn WITHOUT replacement, so every cell's index is evaluated at a FIXED event
# count m -- the count-driven small-sample bias is constant across cells and is
# absorbed by the codmun FE. Tail shares (max-k) are the featured product (they
# have no unbiased estimator, unlike HHI); gini is computed but demoted (a
# fixed-m Gini estimates an m-dependent functional, not the population Gini).
# Count series only (events expanded to w==1); NA when n < m. Daily resolution.
# See notes/concentration_measures_reference.md sec.11.
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
rarefy_year = function(doy, w, n_days, m = 20L, B = 200L) {
  dd = if (all(w == 1)) doy else rep(doy, times = as.integer(round(w)))  # -> events
  n  = length(dd)
  na_out = data.frame(max1 = NA_real_, max3 = NA_real_,
                      max7 = NA_real_, gini = NA_real_)
  if (n < m) return(na_out)                # rarefied indices defined for n >= m only

  idx = seq_len(n_days)
  draws = vapply(seq_len(B), function(b) {
    sub  = dd[sample.int(n, m)]            # m events, WITHOUT replacement
    mass = tabulate(sub, nbins = n_days)   # zero-filled daily masses (sum = m)
    top  = sort(mass, decreasing = TRUE)
    xs   = sort(mass)                       # ascending, zero-filled (cf. concentration_year)
    c(top[1] / m,
      sum(top[seq_len(3L)]) / m,
      sum(top[seq_len(7L)]) / m,
      (2 * sum(idx * xs)) / (n_days * m) - (n_days + 1) / n_days)
  }, numeric(4))

  out = rowMeans(draws)
  data.frame(max1 = out[1], max3 = out[2], max7 = out[3], gini = out[4])
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Count-conditional permutation null (the count-robust PRIMARY test). For each
# municipality-year it holds the OBSERVED event count n fixed and redistributes
# n event-days i.i.d. under a smooth reference seasonal law, B times, then
# averages each index -> the "expected index at this n under the typical season".
# The analysis-time outcome is the EXCESS = observed - permutation mean, which
# nets out BOTH the mechanical count effect (evaluated at the TRUE n, with no
# n>=20 truncation -> no induced selection) and the typical seasonal shape.
# Reference law: municipality, pooled over years (primary; codmun-FE-consistent),
# with a microregion fallback for municipalities with < min_events_law total
# events (too thin for a stable own-law); set ref_level="microregion" to use the
# regional law throughout (robustness). See concentration_measures_reference.md
# sec.11. Caveat: the municipality law pools all years incl. the tested one
# (~1/4 weight at 3-4 fire-years); leave-one-year-out is too thin to be stable.
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Circular Gaussian smoother (FFT circular convolution) of a day-of-year
# histogram; sd_days = kernel bandwidth. Removes zero-probability days.
circ_smooth = function(counts, sd_days = 7) {
  n_days = length(counts)
  d  = 0:(n_days - 1)
  cd = pmin(d, n_days - d)                          # circular distance from lag 0
  k  = exp(-0.5 * (cd / sd_days)^2); k = k / sum(k)
  sm = Re(stats::fft(stats::fft(counts) * stats::fft(k), inverse = TRUE)) / n_days
  sm[sm < 0] = 0                                     # FFT round-off
  sm
}

# Permutation-null mean of each index for ONE municipality-year: draw n days from
# ref_p (length n_days, sums to 1), B times; average. Defined for any n >= 1 (no
# truncation). Index formulas mirror concentration_year().
permute_null_year = function(n, ref_p, n_days, B = 499L) {
  na = data.frame(max1 = NA_real_, max3 = NA_real_, max7 = NA_real_,
                  hhi = NA_real_, hhiunb = NA_real_, gini = NA_real_, rbar = NA_real_)
  if (is.na(n) || n < 1) return(na)
  idx = seq_len(n_days)
  cth = cos(2 * pi * idx / n_days); sth = sin(2 * pi * idx / n_days)
  draws = vapply(seq_len(B), function(b) {
    s    = sample.int(n_days, n, replace = TRUE, prob = ref_p)
    mass = tabulate(s, nbins = n_days)
    top  = sort(mass, decreasing = TRUE); xs = sort(mass)
    c(top[1] / n,
      sum(top[seq_len(3L)]) / n,
      sum(top[seq_len(7L)]) / n,
      sum((mass / n)^2),                                             # hhi (raw)
      if (n > 1) sum(mass * (mass - 1)) / (n * (n - 1)) else NA_real_, # hhiunb
      (2 * sum(idx * xs)) / (n_days * n) - (n_days + 1) / n_days,     # gini
      sqrt(sum(mass * cth)^2 + sum(mass * sth)^2) / n)               # rbar
  }, numeric(7))
  out = rowMeans(draws, na.rm = TRUE)
  data.frame(max1 = out[1], max3 = out[2], max7 = out[3],
             hhi = out[4], hhiunb = out[5], gini = out[6], rbar = out[7])
}

# Municipality-year permutation-null panel: conc_{tag}_{index}_cnull columns
# (the permutation-mean of each index). RUNTIME: ~n_cells x B permutations -- the
# heaviest conc step (~10-20 min/series at B=499); lower B or parallelize by UF
# if needed. micro_map = data.frame(codmun, microreg).
build_cnull_panel = function(events, tag, micro_map, n_days = 365L,
                             B = 499L, seed = 20260610, min_events_law = 30L,
                             sd_days = 7, ref_level = "municipality",
                             year_min = 2017L, year_max = 2025L) {
  ev = events %>%
    filter(!is.na(codmun), !is.na(date)) %>%
    left_join(micro_map, by = "codmun") %>%
    mutate(fyear = year(date), doy = pmin(yday(date), n_days)) %>%
    filter(fyear >= year_min, fyear <= year_max, !is.na(doy))

  # reference laws pooled over years: municipality (primary) + microregion (fallback)
  muni = ev %>% group_by(codmun) %>%
    summarise(n_tot = dplyr::n(), hist = list(tabulate(doy, n_days)), .groups = "drop")
  micro = ev %>% filter(!is.na(microreg)) %>% group_by(microreg) %>%
    summarise(hist = list(tabulate(doy, n_days)), .groups = "drop")
  norm_law  = function(h) { s = circ_smooth(h, sd_days); s / sum(s) }
  muni_law  = setNames(lapply(muni$hist,  norm_law), as.character(muni$codmun))
  muni_ntot = setNames(muni$n_tot, as.character(muni$codmun))
  micro_law = setNames(lapply(micro$hist, norm_law), as.character(micro$microreg))

  pick_law = function(cm, mr) {
    cm = as.character(cm); mr = as.character(mr)
    use_muni = ref_level == "municipality" &&
      !is.na(muni_ntot[cm]) && muni_ntot[cm] >= min_events_law
    if (use_muni) muni_law[[cm]]
    else if (!is.na(mr) && !is.null(micro_law[[mr]])) micro_law[[mr]]
    else muni_law[[cm]]                               # last resort: own (thin) law
  }

  cells = ev %>% group_by(codmun, microreg, fyear) %>%
    summarise(n = dplyr::n(), .groups = "drop")

  set.seed(seed)                                      # cells are in sorted key order
  pm = lapply(seq_len(nrow(cells)), function(i) {
    permute_null_year(cells$n[i], pick_law(cells$codmun[i], cells$microreg[i]), n_days, B)
  })
  res = bind_cols(cells %>% select(codmun, year = fyear), bind_rows(pm))

  key = c("codmun", "year")
  mcols = setdiff(names(res), key)
  names(res)[match(mcols, names(res))] = paste0("conc_", tag, "_", mcols, "_cnull")
  res
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# build_coburst_panel(): municipality x year CROSS-municipality CO-BURSTING -- the
# "dispersed fire at the same time" / sec.10(ii) discriminator, as a muni-year
# outcome. Unlike conc_*/disp_* (WITHIN-municipality), this is BETWEEN munis: do
# m's ignition-DAYS coincide with ignition-days in OTHER, spatially-separated
# municipalities (different microregion -> drop shared local weather) MORE than
# m's own season implies?
#   O(d)            = # munis in OTHER microregions with a fire-day on day d.
#   cob_igni_obs    = mean over m's fire-days of O(d).
#   cob_igni_excess = cob_igni_obs - E[.] under a season-matched null that redraws
#                     m's n fire-days from its own DAY-occurrence law (pooled over
#                     years so a single-year event is ~1/n_years weight and is NOT
#                     self-absorbed; microregion fallback < min_events_law, sd 10 d).
#                     >0 = synchronized across separated munis BEYOND season.
#   cob_igni_n      = # fire-days (analysis-time threshold column, like conc_*_n).
# NOTE: nets out the SMOOTH SEASON, not the daily weather field -- a sub-seasonal
# regional dry/wind spell also raises it; full weather-conditioning (the daily
# fire-risk field, sec.10) is a LATER layer. Reduced-form ("consistent with"
# coordination). Validated on synthetic multi-year data (coordinated year > baseline).
# Microregion map = data.frame(codmun, microreg), as in build_cnull_panel.
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_coburst_panel = function(events, micro_map, n_days = 365L, B = 499L,
                               seed = 20260624, min_events_law = 30L, sd_days = 10,
                               year_min = 2017L, year_max = 2025L) {
  ev = events %>%
    filter(!is.na(codmun), !is.na(date)) %>%
    left_join(micro_map, by = "codmun") %>%
    mutate(year = year(date), doy = pmin(yday(date), n_days)) %>%
    filter(year >= year_min, year <= year_max, !is.na(doy))
  md = ev %>% distinct(codmun, microreg, year, doy)          # one row per municipality fire-DAY

  # per-year length-n_days vectors: A[d] = #active munis; per (year,microreg): same-microreg active
  yrs = sort(unique(md$year))
  Avec = lapply(yrs, function(y) { v = numeric(n_days); t = md %>% filter(year == y) %>% count(doy); v[t$doy] = t$n; v })
  names(Avec) = as.character(yrs)
  amr = md %>% count(year, microreg, doy, name = "a")
  amr_split = split(amr, paste0(amr$year, "|", amr$microreg))
  avec_of = function(y, mr) { v = numeric(n_days); t = amr_split[[paste0(y, "|", mr)]]; if (!is.null(t)) v[t$doy] = t$a; v }

  # season laws from DISTINCT fire-days (match the day-based outcome), pooled over years
  muni  = md %>% group_by(codmun) %>% summarise(n_tot = dplyr::n(), hist = list(tabulate(doy, n_days)), .groups = "drop")
  micro = md %>% filter(!is.na(microreg)) %>% group_by(microreg) %>% summarise(hist = list(tabulate(doy, n_days)), .groups = "drop")
  norm_law  = function(h) { s = circ_smooth(h, sd_days); if (sum(s) <= 0) rep(1 / n_days, n_days) else s / sum(s) }
  muni_law  = setNames(lapply(muni$hist,  norm_law), as.character(muni$codmun))
  muni_ntot = setNames(muni$n_tot, as.character(muni$codmun))
  micro_law = setNames(lapply(micro$hist, norm_law), as.character(micro$microreg))
  pick_law = function(cm, mr) { cm = as.character(cm); mr = as.character(mr)
    if (!is.na(muni_ntot[cm]) && muni_ntot[cm] >= min_events_law) muni_law[[cm]]
    else if (!is.na(mr) && !is.null(micro_law[[mr]])) micro_law[[mr]] else muni_law[[cm]] }

  cells = md %>% group_by(codmun, microreg, year) %>% summarise(days = list(doy), .groups = "drop")
  set.seed(seed)
  res = bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(cells)), function(i) {
    y = cells$year[i]; mr = cells$microreg[i]; cm = cells$codmun[i]
    Od = Avec[[as.character(y)]] - avec_of(y, mr)             # #other-microregion munis active, by doy
    Dd = cells$days[[i]]; nD = length(Dd); law = pick_law(cm, mr)
    draws = vapply(seq_len(B), function(b) mean(Od[sample.int(n_days, nD, replace = TRUE, prob = law)]), numeric(1))
    data.frame(codmun = cm, year = y, cob_igni_n = nD,
               cob_igni_obs = mean(Od[Dd]), cob_igni_excess = mean(Od[Dd]) - mean(draws))
  }))
  res
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# build_conc_panel(): municipality x fire-year temporal-concentration panel.
#   events  data.frame with codmun, date (Date), w (mass weight), and optional
#           cnt (event count per row; default 1). Feed EVENT-level rows (one per
#           ignition/hotspot, w=1) OR pre-aggregated DAILY rows with cnt = that
#           day's event count and w = that day's mass (count or union area, e.g.
#           DETER daily). n_events = sum(cnt) drives the threshold; HHI_unb uses
#           the mass total M = sum(w) (= the count when w is counts).
#   tag     series label used in the conc_{tag}_{metric}{binsuffix} schema.
#   bins    first entry is the headline resolution (daily, no suffix); the rest
#           add _b7 / _b15 / _bm columns for HHI/HHI_unb/Gini only.
# year_basis "calendar" (primary) or "prodes" (Aug-Jul robustness variant).
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_conc_panel = function(events, tag, is_count = TRUE,
                            bins = list(1L, 3L, 7L, 15L, "month"),
                            year_basis = "calendar",
                            year_min = 2017L, year_max = 2025L,
                            rarefy_m = NULL, rarefy_B = 200L,
                            rarefy_seed = 20260610) {

  if (!("cnt" %in% names(events))) events$cnt = 1  # event-level default: 1 per row
  ev = events %>% filter(!is.na(codmun), !is.na(date), !is.na(w))

  # within-(fire)year position
  if (year_basis == "prodes") {            # PRODES year: Aug t-1 .. Jul t
    ev = ev %>% mutate(
      fmonth = month(date),
      fyear  = year(date) + (month(date) >= 8),
      n_days = 365L + as.integer(leap_year(fyear)),
      doy    = as.integer(date - make_date(fyear - 1L, 8L, 1L)) + 1L
    )
  } else {                                 # calendar year (primary)
    ev = ev %>% mutate(
      fmonth = month(date),
      fyear  = year(date),
      n_days = 365L + as.integer(leap_year(fyear)),
      doy    = yday(date)
    )
  }
  ev = ev %>% filter(fyear >= year_min, fyear <= year_max)

  one_bin = function(bw) {
    ev %>%
      group_by(codmun, fyear) %>%
      group_modify(~ {
        m = concentration_year(.x$doy, .x$fmonth, .x$w, .x$n_days[1], bw, is_count)
        m$n_events = sum(.x$cnt)  # true event count (rows may be pre-aggregated days)
        m
      }) %>%
      ungroup()
  }

  base = one_bin(bins[[1]])                # headline (daily): every metric

  bin_suffix = function(bw) if (identical(bw, "month")) "_bm" else paste0("_b", bw)
  for (bw in bins[-1]) {                   # coarser bins: only hhi/hhi_unb/gini
    add = one_bin(bw) %>% select(codmun, fyear, hhi, hhi_unb, gini)
    names(add)[3:5] = paste0(c("hhi", "hhi_unb", "gini"), bin_suffix(bw))
    base = left_join(base, add, by = c("codmun", "fyear"))
  }

  # ---- rarefied (count-robust) tail shares + Gini: daily resolution only ------
  # Must run while the panel is still keyed `fyear` so the conc_{tag}_ prefixing
  # below auto-names the columns conc_{tag}_{max1,max3,max7,gini}_rf<m>. One
  # set.seed() before the sequential, sorted-(codmun,fyear) group_modify makes the
  # whole pass reproducible given fixed inputs. See rarefy_year() above.
  if (!is.null(rarefy_m)) {
    stopifnot(is_count)                    # rarefaction defined for count series only
    set.seed(rarefy_seed)
    rf = ev %>%
      group_by(codmun, fyear) %>%
      group_modify(~ rarefy_year(.x$doy, .x$w, .x$n_days[1],
                                 m = rarefy_m, B = rarefy_B)) %>%
      ungroup()
    names(rf)[3:6] = paste0(c("max1", "max3", "max7", "gini"), "_rf", rarefy_m)
    base = left_join(base, rf, by = c("codmun", "fyear"))
  }

  # NOTE: no low-count threshold here -- the raw indices and the event count
  # (n_events -> conc_{tag}_n) are kept for every municipality-year with >=1 event;
  # the >=N threshold is a sample filter applied at analysis time on conc_{tag}_n.

  if (!is_count) base = base %>% select(-matches("^hhi_unb"))  # undefined for area
  base = base %>% rename(year = fyear)
  if (is_count) base = base %>% select(-mass)                  # mass == n for counts

  # rename to conc_{tag}_* schema (n_events -> n; hhi_unb -> hhiunb)
  names(base) = names(base) %>%
    sub("^n_events$", "n", .) %>%
    gsub("hhi_unb", "hhiunb", .)
  key = c("codmun", "year")
  mcols = setdiff(names(base), key)
  names(base)[match(mcols, names(base))] = paste0("conc_", tag, "_", mcols)
  base
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Spatial-dispersion helpers (operate on Albers XY in meters; no grouped-sf).
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Convex-hull area (km^2) from planar coordinates (shoelace on chull vertices).
chull_area_km2 = function(X, Y) {
  if (length(X) < 3) return(0)
  h = grDevices::chull(X, Y)
  x = X[h]; y = Y[h]
  abs(sum(x * c(y[-1], y[1]) - c(x[-1], x[1]) * y)) / 2 / 1e6
}

# Spatial Gini/HHI over a fixed Albers grid of `cell_km`, per municipality-year.
# Cells assigned by integer coordinate flooring (fixed master grid). N_cells uses
# ceil(areamun / cell_area) as a time-invariant denominator (the FE absorbs its
# level; exact st_make_grid intersection is a refinement). HHI is independent of
# the zero cells (they add 0 to the sum of squares); only Gini needs N_cells.
grid_stats = function(df, cell_km, area_lookup) {
  cell_m    = cell_km * 1000
  cell_area = cell_km^2
  df %>%
    mutate(cx = floor(X / cell_m), cy = floor(Y / cell_m)) %>%
    count(codmun, year, cx, cy, name = "ni") %>%
    group_by(codmun, year) %>%
    arrange(ni, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
    mutate(rank_j = row_number()) %>%
    summarise(
      n_pts    = sum(ni),
      occ      = n(),
      ssq      = sum((ni / sum(ni))^2),
      sum_ni2  = sum(ni * (ni - 1)),
      sum_j_ni = sum(rank_j * ni),
      .groups  = "drop"
    ) %>%
    left_join(area_lookup, by = "codmun") %>%
    mutate(
      N_cells      = pmax(occ, ceiling(areamun / cell_area)),
      disp_shhi    = ssq,
      disp_shhiunb = if_else(n_pts > 1, sum_ni2 / (n_pts * (n_pts - 1)), NA_real_),
      # Gini over N_cells bins = (N_cells-occ) zeros (ranks 1..) + occupied counts:
      disp_sgini   = 2 * ((N_cells - occ) * n_pts + sum_j_ni) / (N_cells * n_pts) -
                       (N_cells + 1) / N_cells
    ) %>%
    select(codmun, year, n_pts, disp_sgini, disp_shhi, disp_shhiunb)
}

# Global Moran's I of ignition counts over the grid, queen contiguity within the
# bounding box of the municipality-year's occupied cells. Positive -> high-count
# cells neighbor high-count cells (clustered); ~0 -> no autocorrelation; negative
# -> checkerboard/dispersed. The adjacency-AWARE complement to disp_sgini, which
# is permutation-invariant over cells. NA if <2 cells in the box or zero variance.
moran_grid = function(cx, cy, ni) {
  rcx = cx - min(cx) + 1L
  rcy = cy - min(cy) + 1L
  nr = max(rcx); nc = max(rcy)
  if (nr * nc < 2L) return(NA_real_)
  Mt = matrix(0, nr, nc)
  Mt[cbind(rcx, rcy)] = ni
  N = nr * nc
  Z = Mt - sum(ni) / N
  nbr = function(A) {                          # sum over queen neighbors (zero-padded)
    P = matrix(0, nr + 2L, nc + 2L)
    P[2:(nr + 1L), 2:(nc + 1L)] = A
    S = matrix(0, nr, nc)
    for (dr in -1:1) for (dc in -1:1) if (!(dr == 0L && dc == 0L)) {
      S = S + P[(2:(nr + 1L)) + dr, (2:(nc + 1L)) + dc]
    }
    S
  }
  W = sum(nbr(matrix(1, nr, nc)))              # ordered queen-adjacent pairs
  denom = sum(Z^2)
  if (W == 0 || denom == 0) return(NA_real_)
  (N / W) * sum(Z * nbr(Z)) / denom
}

# Nearest-neighbor / Clark-Evans + Ripley's K(->L) on planar coords (km). Samples
# to `cap` points for the O(n^2) distance matrix in very large municipality-years.
# Grid-free dispersion / distance-based clustering.
nn_stats_xy = function(X, Y, area_km2, cap = 1500L) {
  na_out = data.frame(disp_nnd_km = NA_real_, disp_ce_R = NA_real_,
                      disp_meanpair_km = NA_real_, disp_ripleyL5 = NA_real_,
                      disp_ripleyL10 = NA_real_, disp_ripleyL20 = NA_real_)
  n = length(X)
  if (n < 2) return(na_out)
  if (n > cap) { s = sample.int(n, cap); X = X[s]; Y = Y[s] }
  n_used = length(X)                                         # post-cap count
  D = sqrt(outer(X, X, "-")^2 + outer(Y, Y, "-")^2) / 1000   # km
  diag(D) = Inf
  nnd = mean(apply(D, 1, min))
  diag(D) = NA
  meanpair = mean(D, na.rm = TRUE)
  # CSR expectation must use the SAME point set the NN distance was computed on
  # (the capped sample, if any). Pairing sample NN with the full-n density biased
  # ce_R upward for >cap-ignition municipality-years. (Subsampling still attenuates
  # ce_R toward 1 for those huge groups -- an inherent thinning effect.)
  d_exp = 0.5 * sqrt(area_km2 / n_used)
  # Ripley's K -> L(r)-r deviation at fixed radii (km), edge-uncorrected. >0 means
  # clustered at scale r, <0 dispersed/regular, ~0 CSR. Reuses D; K density uses the
  # same (capped) point set and the municipality area. Edge bias is conservative
  # (undercounts neighbors near the boundary -> attenuates apparent clustering).
  Ldev = function(r) {
    Kr = area_km2 / (n_used * (n_used - 1)) * sum(D <= r, na.rm = TRUE)
    sqrt(Kr / pi) - r
  }
  data.frame(disp_nnd_km = nnd, disp_ce_R = nnd / d_exp, disp_meanpair_km = meanpair,
             disp_ripleyL5 = Ldev(5), disp_ripleyL10 = Ldev(10), disp_ripleyL20 = Ldev(20))
}

# EDGE-CORRECTED Ripley's L over the OBSERVED-extent window (convex hull of the
# points), via spatstat -- the referee-grade spatial fix. The edge-uncorrected
# Ldev above is anti-conservative for DISPERSION (negative L) near boundaries;
# the translation correction removes that bias, and using the observed extent
# (not the municipal boundary) as the reference region removes the A-sensitivity
# of CSR. disp_L_maxdev is the signed max |L(r)-r| over r in [0,20] km -- a single
# MULTI-SCALE summary that replaces cherry-picking one radius. The simulation-
# based global rank-envelope p-value (Myllymaki et al. 2017) is the remaining
# on-machine upgrade. Count-uniform via the same `cap` as nn_stats_xy. Returns
# NA (no crash) if spatstat is unavailable or the hull is degenerate.
ripley_iso_xy = function(X, Y, cap = 1500L) {
  na_out = data.frame(disp_ripleyL5_iso = NA_real_, disp_ripleyL10_iso = NA_real_,
                      disp_ripleyL20_iso = NA_real_, disp_L_maxdev = NA_real_)
  if (!requireNamespace("spatstat.geom", quietly = TRUE) ||
      !requireNamespace("spatstat.explore", quietly = TRUE)) return(na_out)
  n = length(X)
  if (n < 4) return(na_out)
  if (n > cap) { s = sample.int(n, cap); X = X[s]; Y = Y[s] }
  Xk = X / 1000; Yk = Y / 1000                         # m -> km (L in km)
  win = tryCatch(spatstat.geom::convexhull.xy(Xk, Yk), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(win)) return(na_out)
  pp = tryCatch(spatstat.geom::ppp(Xk, Yk, window = win, checkdup = FALSE),
                error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(pp) || pp$n < 4) return(na_out)
  Lr = tryCatch(spatstat.explore::Lest(pp, correction = "translate",
                                       r = seq(0, 20, by = 0.5)),
                error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(Lr) || is.null(Lr$trans)) return(na_out)
  dev = Lr$trans - Lr$r                                # edge-corrected L(r) - r
  # Degenerate L estimate (collinear/duplicated points -> zero-area hull -> all-NaN
  # trans): which.max(abs(dev)) would be integer(0) -> a length-0 column -> the
  # data.frame() row-count crash. Return the well-formed 1-row NA instead.
  if (length(dev) == 0L || all(is.na(dev))) return(na_out)
  at  = function(rr) dev[which.min(abs(Lr$r - rr))]
  imax = which.max(abs(dev))                           # finite -> length 1 guaranteed now
  data.frame(disp_ripleyL5_iso = at(5), disp_ripleyL10_iso = at(10),
             disp_ripleyL20_iso = at(20),
             disp_L_maxdev = dev[imax])                 # signed max-deviation over [0,20]
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# build_disp_panel(): municipality x CALENDAR-year spatial-dispersion panel from
# ignition points. `points_sf` must be in the Albers CRS (proj_wk) with cols
# codmun and obsTime. `area_lookup` = data.frame(codmun, areamun) in km^2.
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_disp_panel = function(points_sf, area_lookup, cell_set = c(10, 5, 20),
                            year_min = 2017L, year_max = 2025L, nn_cap = 1500L,
                            year_basis = c("calendar", "prodes"), tag = NULL) {
  year_basis = match.arg(year_basis)
  # Accept either an sf (ignition / DETER-centroid points) or a plain data.frame
  # that ALREADY carries planar Albers X/Y columns -- the latter lets the hotspot
  # caller avoid holding millions of point geometries in memory. Both inputs must
  # carry `codmun` and `obsTime`.
  if (inherits(points_sf, "sf")) {
    points_sf = points_sf[!sf::st_is_empty(points_sf), ]  # drop EMPTY geoms (st_coordinates would misalign rows)
    XY = sf::st_coordinates(points_sf)
    df = points_sf %>% sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% mutate(X = XY[, 1], Y = XY[, 2])
  } else {
    df = points_sf                                       # X, Y supplied directly
  }
  df = df %>%
    mutate(year = if (year_basis == "prodes") {
      year(obsTime) + as.integer(month(obsTime) >= 8)
    } else {
      year(obsTime)
    }) %>%
    # degenerate/invalid polygons (some DETER alerts) yield NaN centroids -> drop
    # them so chull/grid/NN never see non-finite XY. No-op for real ignition/hotspot points.
    filter(!is.na(codmun), is.finite(X), is.finite(Y), year >= year_min, year <= year_max) %>%
    select(codmun, year, X, Y)

  # convex-hull extent (the literal "wider areas" footprint)
  disp = df %>%
    group_by(codmun, year) %>%
    summarise(disp_n = n(), disp_hull_km2 = chull_area_km2(X, Y), .groups = "drop")

  # spatial Gini/HHI: default cell size (no suffix) + cell-size sweep
  for (k in seq_along(cell_set)) {
    g = grid_stats(df, cell_set[k], area_lookup)
    if (k == 1) {
      disp = left_join(disp, g %>% select(-n_pts), by = c("codmun", "year"))
    } else {
      disp = left_join(
        disp,
        g %>% transmute(codmun, year, !!paste0("disp_sgini_c", cell_set[k]) := disp_sgini),
        by = c("codmun", "year")
      )
    }
  }

  # Moran's I (cell contiguity) at the default cell size -- the adjacency-aware
  # complement to disp_sgini (which ignores cell arrangement). Queen weights over
  # the bounding box of the municipality-year's occupied cells.
  moran_df = df %>%
    mutate(cx = floor(X / (cell_set[1] * 1000)), cy = floor(Y / (cell_set[1] * 1000))) %>%
    count(codmun, year, cx, cy, name = "ni") %>%
    group_by(codmun, year) %>%
    summarise(disp_moran = moran_grid(cx, cy, ni), .groups = "drop")
  disp = left_join(disp, moran_df, by = c("codmun", "year"))

  # Clark-Evans / NN + Ripley's L -- need >=2 points (n<2 -> NA); no low-count
  # threshold here (applied at analysis time on disp_n).
  keep = disp %>% filter(disp_n >= 2) %>% select(codmun, year)
  area_vec = setNames(area_lookup$areamun, as.character(area_lookup$codmun))
  nn = df %>%
    semi_join(keep, by = c("codmun", "year")) %>%
    group_by(codmun, year) %>%
    group_modify(~ nn_stats_xy(
      # `[` not `[[`: a codmun absent from area_lookup yields NA (-> NA ce_R),
      # not a "subscript out of bounds" crash that aborts the whole panel build.
      .x$X, .x$Y, unname(area_vec[as.character(.y$codmun)]), nn_cap
    )) %>%
    ungroup()
  disp = left_join(disp, nn, by = c("codmun", "year"))

  # Edge-corrected Ripley L over the observed extent (Tier C; spatstat, guarded).
  nn_iso = df %>%
    semi_join(keep, by = c("codmun", "year")) %>%
    group_by(codmun, year) %>%
    group_modify(~ ripley_iso_xy(.x$X, .x$Y, nn_cap)) %>%
    ungroup()
  disp = left_join(disp, nn_iso, by = c("codmun", "year"))

  # Raw indices + the event count (disp_n) kept for every municipality-year with
  # >=1 event; the low-count threshold is a sample filter applied at analysis time.
  out = disp %>% mutate(disp_hull_per_n = disp_hull_km2 / disp_n)
  # Optional tag -> prefix every measure column (disp_* -> disp_<tag>_*) so the
  # hotspot / DETER panels join cleanly alongside the ignition disp_* columns.
  if (!is.null(tag)) {
    out = out %>% dplyr::rename_with(
      ~ sub("^disp_", paste0("disp_", tag, "_"), .x),
      .cols = dplyr::starts_with("disp_")
    )
  }
  out
}


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# build_monthly_ignition_indices(): municipality x calendar-month versions of
# the four ignition-distribution outcomes used in the annual results. Timing is
# measured over the zero-filled days of each calendar month. Spatial dispersion
# uses the same fixed Albers grid and municipal-area support as grid_stats().
# The bias-corrected HHIs are pair probabilities and are therefore undefined for
# n < 2; the Ginis are defined for every positive-count municipality-month.
# Keeping those cells as NA, rather than coding them as zero, preserves the
# estimand and makes the much thinner monthly samples explicit downstream.
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_monthly_ignition_indices = function(
  points_sf,
  area_lookup,
  cell_km = 10,
  year_min = 2017L,
  year_max = 2025L
) {
  stopifnot(
    inherits(points_sf, "sf"),
    all(c("codmun", "obsTime") %in% names(points_sf)),
    all(c("codmun", "areamun") %in% names(area_lookup))
  )

  points_sf = points_sf[!sf::st_is_empty(points_sf), ]
  XY = sf::st_coordinates(points_sf)
  events = points_sf %>%
    sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
    mutate(
      X = XY[, 1],
      Y = XY[, 2],
      year = lubridate::year(obsTime),
      month = lubridate::month(obsTime),
      day = lubridate::day(obsTime),
      n_days = as.integer(lubridate::days_in_month(obsTime))
    ) %>%
    filter(
      !is.na(codmun),
      is.finite(X),
      is.finite(Y),
      year >= year_min,
      year <= year_max
    ) %>%
    select(codmun, year, month, day, n_days, X, Y)

  # Timing HHI/Gini over the 28--31 zero-filled days in each month.
  timing = events %>%
    count(codmun, year, month, day, n_days, name = "ni") %>%
    group_by(codmun, year, month) %>%
    arrange(ni, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
    mutate(rank_j = row_number()) %>%
    summarise(
      conc_igni_n = sum(ni),
      occupied_days = n(),
      n_days = first(n_days),
      sum_ni2 = sum(ni * (ni - 1)),
      sum_j_ni = sum(rank_j * ni),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      conc_igni_hhiunb = if_else(
        conc_igni_n > 1,
        sum_ni2 / (conc_igni_n * (conc_igni_n - 1)),
        NA_real_
      ),
      conc_igni_gini =
        2 * ((n_days - occupied_days) * conc_igni_n + sum_j_ni) /
          (n_days * conc_igni_n) - (n_days + 1) / n_days
    ) %>%
    select(codmun, year, month, conc_igni_n,
           conc_igni_hhiunb, conc_igni_gini)

  # Spatial HHI/Gini over the same fixed 10-km Albers grid used annually.
  cell_m = cell_km * 1000
  cell_area = cell_km^2
  spatial = events %>%
    mutate(
      cx = floor(X / cell_m),
      cy = floor(Y / cell_m)
    ) %>%
    count(codmun, year, month, cx, cy, name = "ni") %>%
    group_by(codmun, year, month) %>%
    arrange(ni, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
    mutate(rank_j = row_number()) %>%
    summarise(
      disp_n = sum(ni),
      occupied_cells = n(),
      sum_ni2 = sum(ni * (ni - 1)),
      sum_j_ni = sum(rank_j * ni),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    left_join(area_lookup, by = "codmun")

  if (anyNA(spatial$areamun)) {
    stop("Monthly spatial indices have municipalities without area support.")
  }

  spatial = spatial %>%
    mutate(
      N_cells = pmax(occupied_cells, ceiling(areamun / cell_area)),
      disp_shhiunb = if_else(
        disp_n > 1,
        sum_ni2 / (disp_n * (disp_n - 1)),
        NA_real_
      ),
      disp_sgini =
        2 * ((N_cells - occupied_cells) * disp_n + sum_j_ni) /
          (N_cells * disp_n) - (N_cells + 1) / N_cells
    ) %>%
    select(codmun, year, month, disp_n, disp_shhiunb, disp_sgini)

  count_check = inner_join(
    timing %>% select(codmun, year, month, conc_igni_n),
    spatial %>% select(codmun, year, month, disp_n),
    by = c("codmun", "year", "month")
  )
  stopifnot(
    nrow(count_check) == nrow(timing),
    nrow(count_check) == nrow(spatial),
    all(count_check$conc_igni_n == count_check$disp_n)
  )

  list(timing = timing, spatial = spatial)
}


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# build_spacetime_panel(): municipality x CALENDAR-year WITHIN-municipality
# space-time interaction tests from ignition points -- the within-muni complement
# to the (cross-municipality) co-bursting series. Two complementary readings, each
# from an established R package (not a hand-rolled statistic) and reported as a
# count-robust standardized z against that package's own permutation null:
#
#   (1) MANTEL (threshold-FREE) -- vegan::mantel correlation between the continuous
#       spatial- and temporal-distance matrices over ALL event pairs; sidesteps any
#       binary distance/time cut and reads interaction across the whole scale range.
#       mantel_z = (r - mean(perm)) / sd(perm) > 0 => near-in-space ~ near-in-time.
#         conc_<tag>_mantel_z
#   (2) KNOX (classic single-scale) -- surveillance::knox count of event pairs close
#       in BOTH space (<= eps_s_km) AND time (<= eps_t_days), against a Monte-Carlo
#       time-permutation null. The raw count is count-confounded (~ n^2 pairs), so the
#       readout is the standardized knox_z = (obs - mean(MC)) / sd(MC).
#         conc_<tag>_knox_z
#
# Both z's are standardized against their package's permutation/MC null, so they are
# count-robust and on a comparable scale; NA when vegan / surveillance is unavailable
# (guarded, like the spatstat-based disp_*_iso columns). `points_sf` is an sf in the
# Albers CRS (proj_wk) with cols codmun + obsTime (same input as build_disp_panel;
# Albers units are meters). The Knox eps_s_km / eps_t_days = 5 km / 3 days match the
# 5 km Ripley radius and the 3-day peak-share ("Day-of-Fire" burst) window. n_cap
# subsamples very large municipality-years so the O(n^2) distance work stays tractable.
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
spacetime_stats_xy = function(x, y, doy, eps_s_km = 5, eps_t_days = 3, B = 199L) {
  na = data.frame(knox_z = NA_real_, mantel_z = NA_real_)
  n = length(x)
  if (n < 4L) return(na)                        # need a few events for a stable null
  have_v = requireNamespace("vegan", quietly = TRUE)
  have_s = requireNamespace("surveillance", quietly = TRUE)
  if (!have_v && !have_s) return(na)
  ds = stats::dist(cbind(x, y)) / 1000           # km, lower-triangle dist object
  dt = stats::dist(doy)                          # days
  # Mantel (vegan): standardized correlation of continuous space & time distances.
  mantel_z = NA_real_
  if (have_v) {
    m = tryCatch(suppressWarnings(local({
          utils::capture.output(out <- vegan::mantel(ds, dt, method = "pearson",
                                                     permutations = B)); out })),
        error = function(e) NULL)
    if (!is.null(m) && length(m$perm) > 1 && stats::sd(m$perm) > 0)
      mantel_z = (m$statistic - mean(m$perm)) / stats::sd(m$perm)
  }
  # Knox (surveillance): standardized close-in-both-space-and-time count vs MC null.
  knox_z = NA_real_
  if (have_s) {
    k = tryCatch(suppressWarnings(local({
          utils::capture.output(out <- surveillance::knox(dt, ds, eps.t = eps_t_days,
                                  eps.s = eps_s_km, simulate.p.value = TRUE, B = B)); out })),
        error = function(e) NULL)
    if (!is.null(k) && length(k$permstats) > 1 && stats::sd(k$permstats) > 0)
      knox_z = (as.numeric(k$statistic) - mean(k$permstats)) / stats::sd(k$permstats)
  }
  data.frame(knox_z = knox_z, mantel_z = mantel_z)
}

build_spacetime_panel = function(points_sf, B = 199L, year_min = 2017L,
                                 year_max = 2025L, n_cap = 1000L,
                                 seed = 20260610, tag = "igni", ...) {
  if (inherits(points_sf, "sf")) {
    points_sf = points_sf[!sf::st_is_empty(points_sf), ]
    XY = sf::st_coordinates(points_sf)
    df = points_sf %>% sf::st_drop_geometry() %>% mutate(X = XY[, 1], Y = XY[, 2])
  } else {
    df = points_sf                                   # X, Y supplied directly
  }
  df = df %>%
    mutate(year = year(obsTime), doy = pmin(yday(obsTime), 365L)) %>%
    filter(!is.na(codmun), is.finite(X), is.finite(Y), !is.na(doy),
           year >= year_min, year <= year_max) %>%
    select(codmun, year, X, Y, doy)

  # Deterministic per-cell seed (sorted key order) so the build is reproducible
  # regardless of grouping order, and each cell's permutation null is independent.
  cells = df %>% distinct(codmun, year) %>% arrange(codmun, year) %>%
    mutate(.seed = seed + dplyr::row_number())

  out = df %>%
    inner_join(cells, by = c("codmun", "year")) %>%
    group_by(codmun, year) %>%
    # Explicit function(.x, .y), NOT a `~` formula: inside a purrr ~ lambda the
    # `...` would forward the lambda's own args (.x = group data, .y = key) rather
    # than this function's dots, silently passing the group tibble as knox_delta_km.
    group_modify(function(.x, .y) {
      set.seed(.x$.seed[1])
      d = .x
      if (nrow(d) > n_cap) d = d[sample.int(nrow(d), n_cap), , drop = FALSE]  # cap O(n^2)
      spacetime_stats_xy(d$X, d$Y, d$doy, B = B, ...)
    }) %>%
    ungroup()

  key = c("codmun", "year")
  mcols = setdiff(names(out), key)
  names(out)[match(mcols, names(out))] = paste0("conc_", tag, "_", mcols)
  out
}


# Municipality -> microregion (IBGE 2017 *regiao geografica imediata*, RGI,
# cod_rgi; the official successor to the *microrregiao*). Used downstream as
# a cluster key for SE inference: municipalities nest within RGIs, so the
# microregion cluster already absorbs within-municipality serial correlation
# (Cameron-Gelbach-Miller 2011).
# https://www.ibge.gov.br/geociencias/organizacao-do-territorio/divisao-regional/15778-divisoes-regionais-do-brasil.html?=&t=downloads
microreg_lookup = readxl::read_excel(
  paste0(DRAW, "IBGE/regioes_geograficas_composicao_por_municipios_2017_20180911.xlsx")
) %>%
  transmute(
    codmun = as.numeric(CD_GEOCODI),
    microreg = as.character(cod_rgi)
  ) %>%
  distinct(codmun, .keep_all = TRUE)
```

```{r 1}
# Latitude and Longitude (old convention: municipal polygon centroids)

# Active convention: IBGE's published municipal-seat points. The same points
# define latitude, longitude and both distances below. The IBGE archive carries
# one `<codmun>_localidades_2022.kml` file and one "Sede Municipal" point per
# municipality. Mojuí dos Campos is already merged
# into Santarém in `zones`, so the combined panel unit inherits Santarém's seat.
localidades_zip = paste0(DRAW, "IBGE/Localidades_Municipios_kml.zip")
localidades_files = unzip(localidades_zip, list = TRUE)$Name
localidades_files = localidades_files[
  grepl("_localidades_2022\\.kml$", localidades_files)
]
localidades_codes = as.numeric(sub(
  ".*_(\\d{7})_localidades_2022\\.kml$",
  "\\1",
  localidades_files
))

panel_codes = zones[[which(zones_prefixes == "mun")]]$zone %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  transmute(codmun = as.numeric(codmun)) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  arrange(codmun) %>%
  pull(codmun)

seat_index = match(panel_codes, localidades_codes)

read_municipal_seat = function(file, codmun) {
  seat = st_read(
    paste0("/vsizip/", localidades_zip, "/", file),
    quiet = TRUE
  ) %>%
    st_zm() %>%
    st_transform(4674)

  stopifnot(
    nrow(seat) == 1,
    as.character(st_geometry_type(seat)[1]) == "POINT"
  )
  coordinates = st_coordinates(seat)[1, ]

  tibble(
    codmun = codmun,
    lat = coordinates[["Y"]],
    lon = coordinates[["X"]]
  )
}

latlong = Map(
  read_municipal_seat,
  localidades_files[seat_index],
  panel_codes
) %>%
  bind_rows() %>%
  arrange(codmun)

stopifnot(
  nrow(latlong) == 772,
  n_distinct(latlong$codmun) == 772,
  !anyNA(latlong)
)

rm(localidades_files, localidades_codes, panel_codes, seat_index, read_municipal_seat)
```
