## 13. COMMODITY PRICES

```{r 13-commodity-prices}
# SEAB-PR / DERAL SIMA daily quotations, Parana. Parana is used because it is
# outside the Amazon, so the price series cannot respond to Amazon clearing --
# the same reasoning Assuncao et al. and Araujo et al. give for their own
# Parana-based indices.
#
# Archives: https://www.agricultura.pr.gov.br/Pagina/Historico-Sima
# Local:    data/raw/SEAB-PR/<year>/...
#
# The archive layout changed three times, so file DISCOVERY is unified here
# while the parsing below is unchanged:
#   2016-2022  one multi-sheet workbook per month, ONE SHEET PER BUSINESS DAY,
#              the date sitting in the penultimate header cell
#   2023-2024  a folder of daily files per month, date in the filename
#   2025       adds a numbered folder level and a "-impressao" print duplicate
#              of every file, which must be dropped or every day is counted twice
# Filenames also drift within years (2021 has "base abril.xls", "outubro
# Base.xls"), so nothing keys off the month name. Every .xls under the year
# folder is discovered and the FILENAME decides which parser applies.

SIMA_DIR <- paste0(DRAW, "SEAB-PR")
KEEP <- "^Boi|^Soja|^Mandioca|^Arroz|^Milho"

# one sheet -> tidy rows. Identical to the original: skip 3, rename the first and
# antepenultimate columns, take the value one row down, keep the five commodities.
sima_sheet <- function(file, sheet, dat) {
  aux <- suppressMessages(read_excel(file, sheet = sheet, skip = 3))
  if (ncol(aux) < 3) return(NULL)
  # The 2025 workbooks are padded out to 68 columns with trailing all-zero /
  # all-blank filler, so a raw ncol(aux) - 2 lands in the padding rather than on
  # the "Media" column and returns 0 for every price. Trim trailing junk columns
  # first; on an untrimmed 2024 sheet this is a no-op.
  junk <- vapply(aux, function(c) {
    v <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(c)))
    all(is.na(c) | trimws(as.character(c)) == "") || all(is.na(v) | v == 0)
  }, logical(1))
  # A wholly empty sheet makes which(!junk) empty, and max() of that is -Inf,
  # which then makes seq_len() throw. Fevereiro2019.xls sheet '08' is exactly
  # this, and the error propagated up and discarded all 20 sheets of the file.
  keep <- which(!junk)
  if (!length(keep)) return(NULL)
  aux <- aux[, seq_len(max(keep)), drop = FALSE]
  if (ncol(aux) < 3) return(NULL)
  colnames(aux)[c(1, ncol(aux) - 2)] <- c("commodity", "price")
  aux %>%
    mutate(price = as.numeric(lead(price, 1))) %>%
    filter(grepl(KEEP, commodity)) %>%
    select(commodity, price) %>%
    mutate(commodity = word(commodity, 1),
           year = year(dat), month = month(dat), day = day(dat))
}

sima_files <- function(y) {
  f <- list.files(file.path(SIMA_DIR, y), pattern = "\\.xls[xm]?$",
                  recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)
  # 2025 ships a "-impressao" print copy of every file plus a handful of
  # " - Copia" duplicates; both would double-weight the days they cover.
  f[!grepl("impressao|c[oó]pia", f, ignore.case = TRUE)]
}

# Daily files are named DD-MM-YYYY from April 2023 onward but DD-MM-YY in
# January to March 2023. Without the two-digit case those 59 files fail the
# daily test, fall through to the workbook parser, and have their sheets
# re-read -- which is where 346 duplicated commodity-days came from.
sima_file_date <- function(b) {
  if (grepl("^[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{4}", b))
    return(as.Date(substr(b, 1, 10), format = "%d-%m-%Y"))
  if (grepl("^[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}([^0-9]|$)", b))
    return(as.Date(substr(b, 1, 8), format = "%d-%m-%y"))
  as.Date(NA)
}

cmdty_prices <- tibble(); failed <- character()

for (ano in 2016:2024) {
  files <- sima_files(ano)
  message(sprintf("SIMA %d: %d files", ano, length(files)))
  for (f in files) {
    b <- basename(f)
    fdate <- sima_file_date(b)
    got <- try({
      if (!is.na(fdate)) {
        sima_sheet(f, 1, fdate)                       # one day per file
      } else {                                        # multi-sheet workbook
        bind_rows(lapply(excel_sheets(f), function(s) {
          # as.Date() with tryFormats ERRORS rather than returning NA when no
          # format matches, so a single non-date sheet header would otherwise
          # take the whole workbook down with it -- that is exactly how
          # February 2019 was silently lost. Parse per sheet, inside try().
          d <- try({
            hdr <- colnames(suppressMessages(read_excel(f, sheet = s)))
            as.Date(hdr[length(hdr) - 1], tryFormats = c("%d-%m-%Y", "%d/%m/%Y"))
          }, silent = TRUE)
          if (inherits(d, "try-error") || length(d) == 0 || is.na(d)) return(NULL)
          # sima_sheet() is wrapped too: one unreadable sheet must cost that
          # sheet, never the whole workbook.
          r <- try(sima_sheet(f, s, d), silent = TRUE)
          if (inherits(r, "try-error")) NULL else r
        }))
      }
    }, silent = TRUE)
    if (inherits(got, "try-error") || is.null(got)) failed <- c(failed, f)
    else cmdty_prices <- bind_rows(cmdty_prices, got)
  }
}
message(sprintf("parsed %d daily quotations; %d files failed", nrow(cmdty_prices), length(failed)))
if (length(failed)) message("  first failures: ", paste(head(basename(failed), 5), collapse = ", "))

# Safety net. Every known duplicate source is excluded above, but a silent
# double-count is the one failure mode that never surfaces as an error.
cmdty_prices <- cmdty_prices %>% distinct(commodity, year, month, day, .keep_all = TRUE)
saveRDS(cmdty_prices, paste0(DV, "cmdty_price_daily.RDS"))

cmdty_monthly <- cmdty_prices %>%
  mutate(year = ifelse(year < 100, year + 2000, year)) %>%
  group_by(commodity, year, month) %>%
  summarise(price = mean(price, na.rm = TRUE), n_days = n(), .groups = "drop")

# Deflator. The original used IGP-DI from an rawdata/igp-di.xls that is not in
# the repository; IPCA is used instead. Both are general price indices and the
# choice is second order here, but the substitution is recorded rather than
# silent.
#
# The series is pulled once from IBGE SIDRA (table 1737, variable 63: monthly
# IPCA percent variation) and cached next to the analysis panels, because
# starlink_results.Rmd reads it too and must not depend on a raw download. IBGE
# revises the series, so a rebuild here changes the deflator: delete the cache
# deliberately rather than as routine housekeeping.
ipca_path = paste0(DFINAL, "ipca_mensal_sidra.csv")
if (!file.exists(ipca_path)) {
  message("fetching IPCA from SIDRA table 1737 ...")
  sidra_url = paste0(
    "https://apisidra.ibge.gov.br/values/t/1737/n1/all/v/63/p/201601-202412"
  )
  sidra_resp = httr::GET(sidra_url, httr::timeout(180))
  stopifnot(httr::status_code(sidra_resp) == 200)
  sidra_ipca = jsonlite::fromJSON(
    httr::content(sidra_resp, "text", encoding = "UTF-8"),
    simplifyDataFrame = TRUE
  )[-1, ]
  ipca_out = tibble(
    period = sidra_ipca$D3C,
    variacao_mensal = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(sidra_ipca$V))
  ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(variacao_mensal)) %>%
    mutate(
      ano = as.integer(substr(period, 1, 4)),
      mes = as.integer(substr(period, 5, 6))
    ) %>%
    select(ano, mes, variacao_mensal) %>%
    arrange(ano, mes)
  stopifnot(
    nrow(ipca_out) == 108,
    min(ipca_out$ano) == 2016,
    max(ipca_out$ano) == 2024,
    min(ipca_out$period) == "201601",
    max(ipca_out$period) == "202412"
  )
  write.csv(ipca_out, ipca_path, row.names = FALSE)
  rm(sidra_url, sidra_resp, sidra_ipca, ipca_out)
}

igp <- read_csv(ipca_path, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  filter(!is.na(variacao_mensal)) %>%
  arrange(ano, mes) %>%
  mutate(index = cumprod(1 + variacao_mensal / 100)) %>%
  filter(ano >= 2016, ano <= 2024) %>%
  transmute(year = as.numeric(ano), month = as.numeric(mes),
            factor = last(index) / index)          # to December 2024 prices

cmdty <- cmdty_monthly %>%
  left_join(igp, by = c("year", "month")) %>%
  mutate(price = price * factor,
         commodity = case_when(
           commodity == "Boi"      ~ "cattle",
           commodity == "Arroz"    ~ "rice",
           commodity == "Mandioca" ~ "cassava",
           commodity == "Milho"    ~ "corn",
           commodity == "Soja"     ~ "soy")) %>%
  select(-factor)

attr(cmdty, "price_base") = "December 2024 BRL"
saveRDS(cmdty, paste0(DFINAL, "cmdty_price_monthly.RDS"))

# Annual, on both year conventions
cmdty_anonormal <- cmdty %>% filter(year >= 2017, year <= 2024) %>%
  group_by(commodity, year) %>% summarise(price = mean(price), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = "commodity", names_prefix = "price_", values_from = "price")

cmdty_anoprodes <- cmdty %>% mutate(year = ifelse(month >= 8, year + 1, year)) %>%
  # The selected specifications use calendar-year prices lagged in the results
  # script. Do not create a partial PRODES-2025 price from Aug--Dec 2024.
  filter(year >= 2017, year <= 2024) %>%
  group_by(commodity, year) %>% summarise(price = mean(price), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = "commodity", names_prefix = "price_", values_from = "price")

attr(cmdty_anonormal, "price_base") = "December 2024 BRL"
attr(cmdty_anoprodes, "price_base") = "December 2024 BRL"
saveRDS(cmdty_anonormal, paste0(DFINAL, "cmdty_price_anonormal.RDS"))
saveRDS(cmdty_anoprodes, paste0(DV, "cmdty_price_anoprodes.RDS"))
rm(cmdty_monthly, igp, cmdty_anonormal, cmdty_anoprodes)
```

## 14. POTENTIAL SOY YIELD

```{r 14-potential-soy-yield}
# -GAEZ v5 (historical 2001-2020)
# [X] RES05-YXX.HP0120.AGERA5.HIST.SOY.HRLM: Attainable kg/ha (high-tech)

# Potential gains over non-croplands (high-tech)
# média entre grid yields (kg/ha) para obter a nível municipal
# multiplicar por hectares totais -> produção alcançável a nível municipal
# normalizar novamente a nível de hectare

# CRS: SIRGAS 2000 Projeção Equivalente de Albers (oficial do IBGE para área)
# https://biblioteca.ibge.gov.br/visualizacao/livros/liv102169.pdf
proj_wk = 'PROJCS["Conica_Equivalente_de_Albers_Brasil",  
  GEOGCS["GCS_SIRGAS2000",  
    DATUM["D_SIRGAS2000",  
      SPHEROID["Geodetic_Reference_System_of_1980",6378137,298.2572221009113]],  
    PRIMEM["Greenwich",0],  
    UNIT["Degree",0.017453292519943295]],  
  PROJECTION["Albers"],  
  PARAMETER["standard_parallel_1",-2],  
  PARAMETER["standard_parallel_2",-22],  
  PARAMETER["latitude_of_origin",-12],  
  PARAMETER["central_meridian",-54],  
  PARAMETER["false_easting",5000000],  
  PARAMETER["false_northing",10000000],  
  UNIT["Meter",1]]'

# Polygons now come from the zones list and are already in proj_wk (Albers),
# so no reprojection is needed. The `id = row_number()` column the old code
# added is dropped: nothing in this section uses it (the extractions bind by
# row order), and it would otherwise survive into soy_potential.RDS.
#
# amz is cut to codmun/namemun/uf to reproduce the old shapefile's column set.
# The save at the end of this section drops namemun, uf and the area_* columns,
# leaving codmun alone, so zones' extra areamun/pop would otherwise leak through.
amz = zones[[which(zones_prefixes == "mun")]]$zone %>%
  select(codmun, namemun, uf) %>%
  st_make_valid()

# zones' uc holds one row per conservation unit, where `year` is the unit's
# establishment year and not a panel year, so the group_by(codmun) below is
# still correct and nothing is double-counted.
uc = zones[[which(zones_prefixes == "uc")]]$zone %>%
  st_make_valid()

ti = zones[[which(zones_prefixes == "ti")]]$zone %>%
  st_make_valid()


# Função para cálculo do valor agregado dentro de um polígono (município)
# exact_extract com 'coverage_area = T' retorna, para cada polígono, um df com:
#   - N observações de grids que fazem intersercção com o polígono
#   - value: valor do raster (como temperatura, precipitação, etc.)
#   - coverage_area: área preenchida pelo grid dentro do polígono
#  Se utilizasse coverage_area = F (padrão), retorna 'coverage_fraction' que é
#  quanto cada grid é preenchido pelo polígono.
sum_yield_prod = function(x) {
  list(
    x %>%
      mutate(
        coverage_area = coverage_area * 1e-4, # m2 -> ha
        total_area = sum(coverage_area, na.rm = T),
        proportion = coverage_area / total_area,
        value = value / ifelse(alias != "act", 1000, 1),
        yield = value * proportion, # yield (prod / ha)
        prod = yield * coverage_area # (in kg or ton)
      ) %>%
      select(yield, prod, coverage_area)
  )
}


# The GAEZ rasters live in the shared data folder, not the old project-local
# rawdata/soy. With the stale path this list came back empty, the loop never
# ran, and soy_potential.RDS was written with codmun and nothing else.
SOY_DIR = paste0(DRAW, "FAO-GAEZ")
files = list.files(SOY_DIR, pattern = "\\.tif$")
stopifnot(length(files) > 0)  # empty: GAEZ soy-yield rasters missing from SOY_DIR
files = files[grepl("YXX", files) | grepl("YLD", files) & grepl("RES06", files)]
soy = tibble(amz %>% st_drop_geometry()) %>%
  left_join(
    ti %>%
      st_drop_geometry() %>%
      group_by(codmun) %>%
      summarise(areati = sum(areati)) %>%
      ungroup(),
    by = "codmun"
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    uc %>%
      st_drop_geometry() %>%
      group_by(codmun) %>%
      summarise(areauc = sum(areauc)) %>%
      ungroup(),
    by = "codmun"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    areati = ifelse(is.na(areati), 0, areati),
    areauc = ifelse(is.na(areauc), 0, areauc)
  ) %>%
  # -any_of("id") rather than -id: the municipal layer in `zones` carries
  # codmun/namemun/uf/areamun/pop and has no `id`, so the bare -id stopped with
  # "Column `id` doesn't exist". any_of() drops it when present and is a no-op
  # when it is not, so this works against either vintage of the layer.
  select(namemun, codmun, uf, everything(), -any_of("id"))

for (f in files) {
  alias = case_when(
    grepl("YCX", f) ~ "cur",
    grepl("YXX", f) ~ "ful",
    grepl("WSR", f) ~ "act",
    T ~ "",
  )

  hl = case_when(
    grepl("HRLM", f) ~ "_high",
    grepl("LRLM", f) ~ "_low",
    T ~ ""
  )

  tif = terra::rast(file.path(SOY_DIR, f)) %>% terra::project(proj_wk)

  # Munic
  ext = exactextractr::exact_extract(
    tif,
    amz,
    coverage_area = T,
    summarize_df = T,
    fun = sum_yield_prod
  )

  soy = bind_cols(
    soy,
    round(sapply(ext, function(df) sum(df[["yield"]], na.rm = TRUE)), 4),
    round(sapply(ext, function(df) sum(df[["prod"]], na.rm = TRUE)), 4),
    round(
      sapply(ext, function(df) {
        sum(df[["coverage_area"]] * !is.nan(df[["yield"]]), na.rm = TRUE)
      }),
      4
    )
  )
  colnames(soy)[(ncol(soy) - 2):ncol(soy)] = c(
    paste0("soyield_", alias, "_mun", hl),
    paste0("soyprod_", alias, "_mun", hl),
    paste0("area_", alias, "_mun", hl)
  )

  # UC
  ext = exactextractr::exact_extract(
    tif,
    uc,
    coverage_area = T,
    summarize_df = T,
    fun = sum_yield_prod
  )
  ext = bind_cols(
    uc %>% st_drop_geometry(),
    sapply(ext, function(df) sum(df[["yield"]], na.rm = TRUE)),
    sapply(ext, function(df) sum(df[["prod"]], na.rm = TRUE)),
    sapply(ext, function(df) {
      sum(df[["coverage_area"]] * !is.nan(df[["yield"]]), na.rm = TRUE)
    })
  )
  colnames(ext)[(ncol(ext) - 2):ncol(ext)] = c("soyield", "soyprod", "area")
  ext = ext %>%
    group_by(codmun) %>%
    summarise(
      soyield = weighted.mean(soyield, w = area),
      soyprod = sum(soyprod),
      area = sum(area),
    ) %>%
    ungroup()
  colnames(ext) = c(
    "codmun",
    paste0("soyield_", alias, "_uc", hl),
    paste0("soyprod_", alias, "_uc", hl),
    paste0("area_", alias, "_uc", hl)
  )
  soy = left_join(soy, ext, by = join_by(codmun))
  soy[[ncol(soy)]] = round(
    ifelse(is.na(soy[[ncol(soy)]]), 0, soy[[ncol(soy)]]),
    4
  )
  soy[[ncol(soy) - 1]] = round(
    ifelse(is.na(soy[[ncol(soy) - 1]]), 0, soy[[ncol(soy) - 1]]),
    4
  )
  soy[[ncol(soy) - 2]] = round(
    ifelse(is.na(soy[[ncol(soy) - 2]]), 0, soy[[ncol(soy) - 2]]),
    4
  )

  # TI
  ext = exactextractr::exact_extract(
    tif,
    ti,
    coverage_area = T,
    summarize_df = T,
    fun = sum_yield_prod
  )
  ext = bind_cols(
    ti %>% st_drop_geometry(),
    sapply(ext, function(df) sum(df[["yield"]], na.rm = TRUE)),
    sapply(ext, function(df) sum(df[["prod"]], na.rm = TRUE)),
    sapply(ext, function(df) {
      sum(df[["coverage_area"]] * !is.nan(df[["yield"]]), na.rm = TRUE)
    })
  )
  colnames(ext)[(ncol(ext) - 2):ncol(ext)] = c("soyield", "soyprod", "area")
  ext = ext %>%
    group_by(codmun) %>%
    summarise(
      soyield = weighted.mean(soyield, w = area),
      soyprod = sum(soyprod),
      area = sum(area),
    ) %>%
    ungroup()
  colnames(ext) = c(
    "codmun",
    paste0("soyield_", alias, "_ti", hl),
    paste0("soyprod_", alias, "_ti", hl),
    paste0("area_", alias, "_ti", hl)
  )
  soy = left_join(soy, ext, by = join_by(codmun))
  soy[[ncol(soy)]] = round(
    ifelse(is.na(soy[[ncol(soy)]]), 0, soy[[ncol(soy)]]),
    4
  )
  soy[[ncol(soy) - 1]] = round(
    ifelse(is.na(soy[[ncol(soy) - 1]]), 0, soy[[ncol(soy) - 1]]),
    4
  )
  soy[[ncol(soy) - 2]] = round(
    ifelse(is.na(soy[[ncol(soy) - 2]]), 0, soy[[ncol(soy) - 2]]),
    4
  )
}


saveRDS(
  soy %>% select(-namemun, -uf, -starts_with("area")),
  paste0(DV, "soy_potential.RDS")   # was intermediarydata/; section 16 reads this path
)
rm(soy)
```

## 15. PASTURE SUITABILITY

```{r 15-pasture-suitability}
# Cattle-rent analog to the soy-potential layer of section 14. Motivation: fire
# scars are 73% of the DETER degradation outcome, and fire is the pasture
# establishment and maintenance tool, so grazing potential is at least as
# mechanism-relevant as soy potential for a fire-driven degradation outcome.
#
# Source: FGGD "Suitability of global land area for pasture", FAO catalog record
#   2b357400-891a-11db-b9b2-000d939bc5d8, file Map6_56.zip.
#   Method: von Velthuizen et al. (FAO and IIASA, 2007) â€” the same FAO/IIASA
#   lineage as the GAEZ soy layer, so the pair is methodologically consistent.
#   5 arc-minutes, WGS84, global, 2005 version.
#
# Deliberately the "global land area" layer, NOT the sibling "currently available
# land" layer. The latter zeroes urban, closed-forest and irrigated pixels, and
# closed forest is exactly where our degradation occurs â€” it would measure
# pasture potential on already-cleared land and act as an inverse forest-cover
# index. (The pair of layers IS useful as a frontier-vs-intensification
# heterogeneity test, but that is a mechanism test, not a control.)

# ESRI ArcInfo Binary Grid, not a GeoTIFF: point terra at the *directory*, and
# keep the sibling info/ folder or the grid will not open.
past = terra::rast(paste0(DRAW, "FAO-GAEZ/fggd_pasture/pasture_si"))

# -997 is a nodata sentinel, not a suitability value (1.2% of Amazon-area cells).
# Mask it BEFORE any zonal statistic, otherwise municipal means are dragged down,
# worst on varzea municipalities carrying a lot of water.
past = terra::classify(past, cbind(-997, NA))

# Values are a continuous index on 0-10000 (10,002 distinct levels globally),
# not a coarse suitability class. Divide by 10000 for a 0-1 index; kept on the
# native scale because the control enters interacted with year under
# municipality fixed effects, which absorbs any linear rescaling.
past = terra::project(past, proj_wk)

# Area-weighted municipal mean, same approach as section 14: equal-area
# projection first, then weight each grid cell by the area it covers inside the
# polygon.
pasture = tibble(
  codmun = amz$codmun,
  pasture_suit_mun = round(
    exactextractr::exact_extract(
      past,
      amz,
      fun = "weighted_mean",
      weights = "area",
      progress = FALSE
    ),
    4
  )
)

saveRDS(pasture, paste0(DV, "pasture_suitability.RDS"))
rm(past, pasture)
```

## 16. JOINING DATASETS

```{r 16-joining-datasets}
# GUARD: every intermediate joined below must already sit on the MERGED
# municipal grid (Santarem + Mojui = one unit, section 0). A file still carrying
# Mojui's own codmun was produced BEFORE the merge; joining it would silently
# DROP those rows, and the merged unit would lose that variable's Mojui share.
# Fail loudly and name the sections to re-run instead.
stale_premerge = Filter(
  function(f) {
    x = readRDS(f)
    is.data.frame(x) && "codmun" %in% names(x) &&
      any(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(x$codmun)) == MOJUI_CODMUN, na.rm = TRUE)
  },
  c(
    list.files(DV, pattern = "_(normalyr|prodesyr)\\.RDS$", full.names = TRUE),
    # every non-suffixed file this chunk joins; audited against the chunk's own
    # active read list on 2026-08-03. The commented monthly-panel block below
    # reads *_monthly.RDS - if it is ever re-enabled, add those here too.
    Filter(file.exists, file.path(DV,
      c("munic.RDS", "mb_forest.RDS", "soy_potential.RDS",
        "pasture_suitability.RDS", "factions.RDS", "mbtrans.RDS",
        "prodes_full.RDS", "spei12_copernicus_era5_normalyr.RDS",
        "spei12_copernicus_era5_prodesyr.RDS")))
  )
)
if (length(stale_premerge) > 0) stop(
  "Pre-merge intermediates still carry Mojui dos Campos (codmun 1504752); ",
  "re-run their sections: ", paste(basename(stale_premerge), collapse = ", ")
)

# Companion guard: everything this chunk joins must EXIST in DV. Without it a
# file left behind in the previous generation fails later as a cryptic join
# error on a missing object, or silently joins nothing.
normal_required = paste0(
  c("starlink", "geosat", "deter", "police", "pmcams",
    "tmax", "prcp", "deaths", "ignimun"),
  "_normalyr.RDS"
)
prodes_required = paste0(
  c("starlink", "geosat", "tmax", "prcp"),
  "_prodesyr.RDS"
)
needed = c(
  "munic.RDS", "mb_forest.RDS", "mbtrans.RDS", "soy_potential.RDS",
  "pasture_suitability.RDS", "factions.RDS", "prodes_full.RDS",
  "deter_monthly.RDS",
  "spei12_copernicus_era5_normalyr.RDS",
  "spei12_copernicus_era5_prodesyr.RDS",
  normal_required,
  prodes_required,
  # conc_aquaref is NOT required: the AQUA block is off (RUN_AQUA = FALSE in
  # chunk 11) and nothing downstream reads its columns. It is joined below only
  # if a previous build left one behind.
  paste0(c("conc_igni", "disp_igni"), "_normalyr.RDS")
)
missing_dv = needed[!file.exists(file.path(DV, needed))]
if (length(missing_dv) > 0) stop(
  "Missing from ", DV, " (re-run the sections that build them): ",
  paste(missing_dv, collapse = ", ")
)

# ---- forest denominators: fixed 2021, prior year, and the vintage made explicit -
# `area_forest` has always been the 2021 stock -- the join below filtered
# mb_forest to year == 2021 -- but nothing in the NAME said so, and downstream code
# repeatedly had to rediscover that it is time-invariant. Three columns are emitted
# now instead of one:
#   areaforest_2021   the 2021 stock, vintage in the name. Identical to area_forest.
#   area_forest       kept as-is so every existing call site kept working.
#   lag_areaforest    the PRIOR-YEAR stock, areamun x p_forest(t-1).
#
# Why the prior-year column is worth having in the pipeline rather than bolted on
# downstream: the lag needs 2016, which the estimation panels do not carry, so it
# can only be built where mb_forest is still in scope. Doing it later loses 2017 and
# with it a pre-period lead -- which on its own moved the joint pre-trend from 0.076
# to 0.046 in testing, an artifact of the missing year rather than the denominator.
#
# `areaforest_2021` rather than `2021_areaforest`: R names cannot begin with a digit.
#
# CAVEAT to carry into any use of lag_areaforest. It is predetermined with respect
# to the SAME year's outcome but NOT with respect to treatment: the 2023 and 2024
# lagged stocks already embody Starlink's earlier effect, so part of the response
# sits in the denominator. The contamination is small -- the stock moves about 0.7%
# a year -- but it is why the fixed-2021 stock stays the headline denominator and
# the prior-year one is a robustness form.
forest_denoms = readRDS(paste0(DV, "mb_forest.RDS")) %>%
  arrange(codmun, year) %>%
  group_by(codmun) %>%
  mutate(p_forest_lag = dplyr::lag(p_forest)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(codmun, year, p_forest, p_forest_lag)

# ONE ROW BEYOND MapBiomas' last year, carrying only the lag.
#
# mb_forest ends in 2024, so forest_denoms has no 2025 row and the PRODES-year
# panel's 2025 rows join to nothing: lag_areaforest came out NA for all 772
# municipalities, which trips the NormalizationRobustness guard
# `!anyNA(nz_dat$lag_areaforest)` in the results file. The 2024 stock
# needed to form the 2025 lag does exist -- only the row to hang it on was
# missing. This reproduces the correction previously applied out of band to the
# old panels with `year = year + 1L`, now in the pipeline so the patch is no
# longer needed.
#
# p_forest itself stays NA in the added row: there is no 2025 forest stock, only a
# 2024 one to lag. Nothing reads p_forest at that year -- area_forest and
# areaforest_2021 are both the fixed 2021 cross-section.
mb_last = max(forest_denoms$year)
forest_denoms = bind_rows(
  forest_denoms,
  forest_denoms %>%
    filter(year == mb_last) %>%
    transmute(codmun, year = mb_last + 1L, p_forest_lag = p_forest) %>%
    mutate(p_forest = NA_real_)
)

# The 2021 share, as a codmun-keyed cross-section
forest_2021 = forest_denoms %>% filter(year == 2021) %>%
  select(codmun, p_forest_2021 = p_forest)
stopifnot(
  nrow(forest_2021) == n_distinct(forest_denoms$codmun),
  # 2016 must be present or the 2017 lag is NA and the lead is silently lost
  min(forest_denoms$year) <= 2016,
  # every panel year from 2017 through the added row must resolve a lag
  !anyNA(forest_denoms$p_forest_lag[forest_denoms$year >= 2017])
)

add_forest_denoms = function(dat) {
  dat %>%
    left_join(forest_2021, by = "codmun") %>%
    left_join(forest_denoms %>% select(codmun, year, p_forest_lag),
              by = c("codmun", "year")) %>%
    mutate(
      areaforest_2021 = areamun * p_forest_2021,
      # area_forest keeps its historical meaning: the 2021 stock
      area_forest = areaforest_2021,
      lag_areaforest = areamun * p_forest_lag
    )
}

# Section 8 writes a separate endpoint file for each panel. Calendar outcomes
# receive December SPEI-12; PRODES-year outcomes receive July SPEI-12.
spei12_calendar = readRDS(file.path(
  DV, "spei12_copernicus_era5_normalyr.RDS"
)) %>%
  filter(year >= 2017, year <= 2024) %>%
  transmute(
    codmun = as.numeric(codmun),
    year = as.integer(year),
    spei12_dec = as.numeric(spei12_dec)
  )
spei12_prodes = readRDS(file.path(
  DV, "spei12_copernicus_era5_prodesyr.RDS"
)) %>%
  filter(year >= 2017, year <= 2025) %>%
  transmute(
    codmun = as.numeric(codmun),
    year = as.integer(year),
    spei12_jul = as.numeric(spei12_jul)
  )
stopifnot(
  !anyDuplicated(spei12_calendar[c("codmun", "year")]),
  !anyDuplicated(spei12_prodes[c("codmun", "year")]),
  all(is.finite(spei12_calendar$spei12_dec)),
  all(is.finite(spei12_prodes$spei12_jul))
)

# Predetermined fire-scar exposure used by Model II. Carry it on the compact
# panel so the results file does not need the monthly DETER intermediate.
pre2022_fire = readRDS(paste0(DV, "deter_monthly.RDS")) %>%
  filter(year > 2016L | (year == 2016L & month >= 8L), year <= 2021L) %>%
  group_by(codmun) %>%
  summarise(
    pre2022_fire_scar_area = sum(area_mun_deter_degr_fire, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Normal year
ds_normalyr = readRDS(paste0(DV, "munic.RDS")) %>%
    add_forest_denoms() %>%
    left_join(pre2022_fire, by = "codmun") %>%
    mutate(
      pre2022_fire_scar_intensity =
        100 * pre2022_fire_scar_area / area_forest
    ) %>%
    select(-pre2022_fire_scar_area) %>%
    left_join(
      readRDS(paste0(DV, "soy_potential.RDS")),
      by = "codmun"
    ) %>%
    left_join(    # section 15: FGGD grazing potential, cattle-rent analog to soy
      readRDS(paste0(DV, "pasture_suitability.RDS")),
      by = "codmun"
    ) %>%
    # Section A2: 2021 planted-area and herd shares, the OBSERVED exposure
    # weights for the commodity-price channel (soyield_ful_mun_high and
    # pasture_suit_mun above are the POTENTIAL weights). Optional rather than
    # required: A2 pulls from the SIDRA API on its first run, so a panel built
    # before that should not fail -- it just carries no share_ columns.
    left_join(readRDS(paste0(DV, "factions.RDS")), by = "codmun") %>%
    left_join(
      readRDS(paste0(DV, "starlink_normalyr.RDS")),
      by = c("codmun", "year")
    ) %>%
    left_join(
      readRDS(paste0(DV, "geosat_normalyr.RDS")),
      by = c("codmun", "year")
    ) %>%
    left_join(
      readRDS(paste0(DV, "deter_normalyr.RDS")),
      by = c("codmun", "year")
    ) %>%
    left_join(
      readRDS(paste0(DV, "police_normalyr.RDS")),
      by = c("codmun", "year")
    ) %>%
    left_join(
      readRDS(paste0(DV, "pmcams_normalyr.RDS")),
      by = c("codmun", "year")
    ) %>%
    left_join(
      readRDS(paste0(DV, "tmax_normalyr.RDS")),
      by = c("codmun", "year")
    ) %>%
    left_join(
      readRDS(paste0(DV, "prcp_normalyr.RDS")),
      by = c("codmun", "year")
    ) %>%
    left_join(
      spei12_calendar,
      by = c("codmun", "year")
    ) %>%
    left_join(
      readRDS(paste0(DV, "deaths_normalyr.RDS")),
      by = c("codmun", "year")
    ) %>%
    left_join(
      readRDS(paste0(DV, "mbtrans.RDS")),
      by = c("codmun", "year")
    ) %>%
    left_join(
      readRDS(paste0(DV, "ignimun_normalyr.RDS")),
      by = c("codmun", "year")
    ) %>%
    left_join(
      readRDS(paste0(DV, "conc_igni_normalyr.RDS")),
      by = c("codmun", "year")
    ) %>%
    left_join(
      readRDS(paste0(DV, "disp_igni_normalyr.RDS")),
      by = c("codmun", "year")
    ) %>%
    mutate(reg_sample = ifelse(year > 2021, 1, 0)) %>%
    filter(year <= 2024) %>%
    arrange(codmun, year)
stopifnot(
  !anyNA(ds_normalyr$spei12_dec),
  !anyNA(ds_normalyr$pre2022_fire_scar_intensity)
)

# Exact calendar-panel contract. These are the raw outcomes and inputs consumed

missing_normal_columns = setdiff(normal_panel_columns, names(ds_normalyr))
if (length(missing_normal_columns)) {
  stop(

# ---- writing the panel ------------------------------------------------------
# The .RDS is the authoritative copy and keeps the real column names. The .dta
# is written alongside for Stata, with names shortened to fit.
#
# WHY THE SHORTENING IS NEEDED. Stata caps variable names at 32 characters and
# haven::write_dta refuses anything longer. The v2 SICAR masks are named
# `sicar21_large` / `sicar21_small` where v1 used `sicarL` / `sicarS`, seven
# characters more, and that pushes the derived columns over:
#   area_sicar21_large_deter_degr_outr      34
#   disp_igni_sicar21_small_ripleyL20_iso   37
# Rather than cripple the R-side names to satisfy Stata, the abbreviation is
# applied only on the way out. Longest patterns first, so the by-size overlap
# masks are matched before the pooled ones.
stata_names = function(d) {
  n = names(d)
  for (p in list(
    c("over_ndpf_large", "ovNDPFL"), c("over_ndpf_small", "ovNDPFS"),
    c("over_sett_large", "ovSETTL"), c("over_sett_small", "ovSETTS"),
    c("over_ti_large",   "ovTIL"),   c("over_ti_small",   "ovTIS"),
    c("over_uc_large",   "ovUCL"),   c("over_uc_small",   "ovUCS"),
    c("sicar21_large",   "s21L"),    c("sicar21_small",   "s21S"),
    c("sicar21_ca",      "s21C"),
    c("over_ndpf",       "ovNDPF"),  c("over_sett",       "ovSETT"),
    c("over_ti",         "ovTI"),    c("over_uc",         "ovUC")
  )) n = gsub(p[1], p[2], n, fixed = TRUE)
  # backstop for anything still over the limit, keeping names unique
  too_long = nchar(n) > 32
  if (any(too_long)) n[too_long] = make.unique(substr(n[too_long], 1, 30), sep = "_")
  names(d) = n
  d
}

write_panel = function(d, stem) {
  attr(d, "coordinate_basis") = "ibge_municipal_seat"
  attr(d, "faction_report_years") = c(2023L, 2024L)
  attr(d, "faction_time_varying") = FALSE
  saveRDS(d, paste0(DFINAL, stem, ".RDS"))      # authoritative, full names
  ok = tryCatch({ haven::write_dta(stata_names(d), paste0(DFINAL, stem, ".dta")); TRUE },
                error = function(e) { message("  [dta] ", stem, " not written: ",
                                              conditionMessage(e)); FALSE })
  message(sprintf("  wrote %s.RDS (%d x %d)%s", stem, nrow(d), ncol(d),
                  if (ok) " and .dta" else ""))
}

# Write the requested calendar panel through 2024.
write_panel(ds_normalyr, "dataset_normalyr")


# PRODES year: native PRODES 6.25 ha outcomes and required covariates only.
# DETER degradation, enforcement, pollution, mortality, MapBiomas transitions,
# ignition, dispersion, factions, and tenure outcomes are calendar-year analyses.
# They are neither generated on an August--July basis nor joined here.
prodes_outcome_columns = c(
  "area_mun_prodes_defo",
  "area_mun_prodes_defo_cces",
  "area_mun_prodes_defo_ccwv",
  "area_mun_prodes_defo_dpdp",
  "area_mun_prodes_defo_mine",
  "n_mun_prodes_defo",
  "n_mun_prodes_defo_cces",
  "n_mun_prodes_defo_ccwv",
  "n_mun_prodes_defo_dpdp",
  "n_mun_prodes_defo_mine"
)
prodes_native = readRDS(paste0(DV, "prodes_full.RDS")) %>%
  select(codmun, year, all_of(prodes_outcome_columns))

# Predetermined fire susceptibility is a selected control, not a PRODES-year
# outcome. Build it once from the calendar-dated DETER history through 2021 and
# carry the resulting time-invariant municipal intensity on the compact panel.
pre2022_fire_scar = readRDS(paste0(DV, "deter_monthly.RDS")) %>%
  filter(
    year > 2016L | (year == 2016L & month >= 8L),
    year <= 2021L
  ) %>%
  group_by(codmun) %>%
  summarise(
    pre2022_fire_scar_area = sum(area_mun_deter_degr_fire, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ds_prodesyr = readRDS(paste0(DV, "munic.RDS")) %>%
    add_forest_denoms() %>%
    left_join(
      readRDS(paste0(DV, "soy_potential.RDS")),
      by = "codmun"
    ) %>%
    left_join(    # section 15: FGGD grazing potential, cattle-rent analog to soy
      readRDS(paste0(DV, "pasture_suitability.RDS")),
      by = "codmun"
    ) %>%
    left_join(
      readRDS(paste0(DV, "starlink_prodesyr.RDS")),
      by = c("codmun", "year")
    ) %>%
    left_join(
      readRDS(paste0(DV, "geosat_prodesyr.RDS")),
      by = c("codmun", "year")
    ) %>%
    left_join(prodes_native, by = c("codmun", "year")) %>%
    left_join(
      readRDS(paste0(DV, "tmax_prodesyr.RDS")),
      by = c("codmun", "year")
    ) %>%
    left_join(
      readRDS(paste0(DV, "prcp_prodesyr.RDS")),
      by = c("codmun", "year")
    ) %>%
    left_join(
      spei12_prodes,
      by = c("codmun", "year")
    ) %>%
    left_join(pre2022_fire_scar, by = "codmun") %>%
    mutate(
      reg_sample = ifelse(year > 2022, 1, 0),
      pre2022_fire_scar_intensity =
        100 * pre2022_fire_scar_area / area_forest,
      area_mun_prodes_defo_ccut =
        coalesce(area_mun_prodes_defo_cces, 0) +
        coalesce(area_mun_prodes_defo_ccwv, 0),
      n_mun_prodes_defo_ccut =
        coalesce(n_mun_prodes_defo_cces, 0) +
        coalesce(n_mun_prodes_defo_ccwv, 0)
    ) %>%
    filter(year <= 2025) %>%
    arrange(codmun, year) %>%
    select(
      codmun, year, uf, microreg, reg_sample,
      coverarea, starlink,
      areamun, area_forest,
      dens, lat, lon, dist_coast, dist_brasilia,
      way_road_pav, way_rail,
      tmax, prcp, geosat,
      soyield_ful_mun_high, pasture_suit_mun,
      spei12_jul, pre2022_fire_scar_intensity,
      area_mun_prodes_defo,
      area_mun_prodes_defo_ccut,
      area_mun_prodes_defo_cces,
      area_mun_prodes_defo_ccwv,
      area_mun_prodes_defo_dpdp,
      area_mun_prodes_defo_mine,
      n_mun_prodes_defo,
      n_mun_prodes_defo_ccut,
      n_mun_prodes_defo_cces,
      n_mun_prodes_defo_ccwv,
      n_mun_prodes_defo_dpdp,
      n_mun_prodes_defo_mine
    )
stopifnot(
  ncol(ds_prodesyr) == 35L,
  !anyNA(ds_prodesyr$spei12_jul),
  !anyNA(ds_prodesyr$pre2022_fire_scar_intensity)
)

# Write the requested PRODES-year panel through 2025.
write_panel(ds_prodesyr, "dataset_prodesyr")
writeLines(PRODES_LAYER, paste0(DFINAL, "prodes_source.txt"))
```
